TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/mesh/mesh-instances.mdx
==================================================
---
title: MeshInstances
---

Holds the per instance data for `Renderer:drawImageMeshInstanced`. Unlike
the mesh buffers it is meant to be rewritten every frame.


## Methods

### `resize`

{/* resize: (self: MeshInstances, count: number) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
resize(count: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Sets the number of instances.
```lua
local mi = MeshInstances()
mi:resize(3)
```


### `set`

{/* set: (
        self: MeshInstances,
        index: number,
        transform: Mat2D,
        opacity: number?,
        additiveness: number?,
        uvTranslate: Vector?,
        uvScale: Vector?
    ) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
set(index: number, transform: Mat2D, opacity: number?, additiveness: number?, uvTranslate: Vector?, uvScale: Vector?) -> ()
```
</div>

Writes the instance at `index`, which is zero based. Everything past
`transform` is optional.
```lua
local mi = MeshInstances(2)
mi:set(0, Mat2D.withTranslation(Vector.xy(10, 20)))
mi:set(1, Mat2D.identity(), 0.5, 0, Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(0.5, 0.5))
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/gradient/gradient.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Gradient
---

Represents a gradient used for filling or stroking a shape. A gradient is
defined by a set of color stops ([GradientStop](/scripting/api-reference/gradient/gradient-stop)) and either a linear or radial configuration.


## Constructors

### `linear`

{/* linear: (from: Vector, to: Vector, stops: { GradientStop } ) -> Gradient */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
linear(from: Vector, to: Vector, stops: {GradientStop}) -> Gradient
```
</div>

Creates a linear gradient that transitions between the specified color
stops along the line from 'from' to 'to'.

```lua
local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(100, 0), {
  { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
  { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
})
```


### `radial`

{/* radial: (from: Vector, radius: number, stops: { GradientStop } ) -> Gradient */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
radial(from: Vector, radius: number, stops: {GradientStop}) -> Gradient
```
</div>

Creates a radial gradient centered at 'from', extending outward to the
given radius, using the specified color stops.

```lua
local g = Gradient.radial(Vector.xy(50, 50), 40, {
  { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
  { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
})
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/gradient/gradient-stop.mdx
==================================================
---
title: GradientStop
---

A color stop in a [Gradient](/scripting/api-reference/gradient/gradient), defined by its position in the range [0, 1] and
the color at that position.


## Fields

### `position`

Position of the stop along the gradient, where 0 is the start and 1 is
the end.
```lua highlight={3,7}
local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(100, 0), {
    {
        position = 0,
        color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0)
    },
    {
        position = 1,
        color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255)
    },
})
```


### `color`

[Color](/scripting/api-reference/color/color) at the specified position.
```lua highlight={4,8}
local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(100, 0), {
    {
        position = 0,
        color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0)
    },
    {
        position = 1,
        color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255)
    },
})
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/promise/promise.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Promise
---

A value that will be available in the future.
Use `andThen` to register callbacks, or `await` inside `async` to
suspend until the value is ready.
Supports cancellation: call `cancel()` to abort pending work and
propagate cancellation to chained promises.


## Fields

### `andThen`

Register a callback for when the promise fulfills.
The handler may return a value that becomes the next promise's result.


## Constructors

### `new`

{/* new: <T>(executor: (resolve: (value: T) -> (), reject: (error: any) -> (), onCancel: (hook: () -> ()) -> ()) -> ()) -> Promise<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
new(executor: (resolve:(value: T) ->(), reject:(error: any) ->(), onCancel:(hook:() ->()) ->()) ->()) -> Promise<T>
```
</div>

Create a new promise with an executor function.
The executor receives resolve, reject, and onCancel callbacks.


### `resolve`

{/* resolve: <T>(value: T?) -> Promise<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
resolve(value: T?) -> Promise<T>
```
</div>

Create an already-resolved promise. Resolves with nil if no value given.


### `reject`

{/* reject: <T>(error: any?) -> Promise<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
reject(error: any?) -> Promise<T>
```
</div>

Create an already-rejected promise. Error can be any Lua value.
Rejects with "rejected" if no argument is provided.


### `all`

{/* all: <T>(promises: {Promise<T>}) -> Promise<{T}> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
all(promises: {Promise<T>}) -> Promise<{T}>
```
</div>

Wait for all promises to resolve; rejects if any rejects.
On rejection, the remaining promises that nothing else waits on are
cancelled.


## Methods

### `catch`

{/* catch: (self: Promise<T>, onRejected: (error: any) -> any) -> any */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
catch(onRejected: (error: any) -> any) -> any
```
</div>

Register a callback for when the promise rejects.
Errors can be any Lua value (string, table, number, etc.).


### `finally`

{/* finally: (self: Promise<T>, onFinally: () -> ()) -> Promise<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
finally(onFinally: () ->()) -> Promise<T>
```
</div>

Register a callback that runs whether the promise fulfills or rejects.


### `cancel`

{/* cancel: (self: Promise<T>) -> Promise<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
cancel() -> Promise<T>
```
</div>

Cancel this promise. Fires the onCancel hook (if registered),
propagates cancellation down to chained promises, and propagates
up to the parent if all its consumers are cancelled.
No-op if the promise is already settled.


### `onCancel`

{/* onCancel: (self: Promise<T>, hook: () -> ()) -> Promise<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
onCancel(hook: () ->()) -> Promise<T>
```
</div>

Register a cancellation hook that fires when cancel() is called.
Used to clean up in-flight work (e.g. abort a network request).
Replaces any hook registered before.


### `getStatus`

{/* getStatus: (self: Promise<T>) -> string */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
getStatus() -> string
```
</div>

Returns the current state: "Pending", "Fulfilled", "Rejected", or "Cancelled".




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Vector
---

Represents a vector with three components. Vectors created with
`Vector.xy` have z = 0. All magnitude and interpolation operations
(`length`, `dot`, `distance`, `normalized`, `lerp`, ...) use all three
components; with z = 0 they behave exactly as 2D math.


## Fields

### `x`

The x component of the vector (read-only).
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(10, -5)
local xValue = v.x  -- 10
```


### `y`

The y component of the vector (read-only).
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(10, -5)
local yValue = v.y  -- -5
```


### `z`

The z component of the vector (read-only). Zero for vectors created
with `Vector.xy`; populated by 3D APIs that return a [Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector).
```lua
local v = m:transformPoint(1, 2, 3)
local zValue = v.z
```


## Constructors

### `xy`

{/* xy: (x:number, y:number) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
xy(x: number, y: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Creates a vector with the specified x and y components.
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(5, -2)  -- 5 -2
```


### `xyz`

{/* xyz: (x:number, y:number, z:number) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
xyz(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Creates a vector with the specified x, y and z components.
```lua
local v = Vector.xyz(1, 2, 3)
```


### `origin`

{/* origin: () -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
origin() -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the zero vector (0, 0).
```lua
local origin = Vector.origin()  -- 0 0
```


### `cross3`

{/* cross3: (a: Vector, b: Vector) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
cross3(a: Vector, b: Vector) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the 3D cross product of two vectors.
```lua
local z = Vector.cross3(Vector.xyz(1,0,0), Vector.xyz(0,1,0))  -- 0 0 1
```


### `scaleAndAdd`

{/* scaleAndAdd: (a: Vector, b: Vector, scale: number) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
scaleAndAdd(a: Vector, b: Vector, scale: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns a + b * scale.
```lua
local r = Vector.scaleAndAdd(Vector.xy(1,2), Vector.xy(3,4), 2)  -- 7 10
```


### `scaleAndSub`

{/* scaleAndSub: (a: Vector, b: Vector, scale: number) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
scaleAndSub(a: Vector, b: Vector, scale: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns a - b * scale.
```lua
local r = Vector.scaleAndSub(Vector.xy(7,10), Vector.xy(3,4), 2)  -- 1 2
```


### `lerp`

{/* lerp: (from: Vector, to: Vector, t: number) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lerp(from: Vector, to: Vector, t: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the linear interpolation from one vector to another, using t
where 0 returns `from` and 1 returns `to`.
```lua
local p = Vector.lerp(Vector.xy(0,0), Vector.xy(8,0), 0.25)  -- 2 0
```


### `normalized`

{/* normalized: (v: Vector) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
normalized(v: Vector) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns a normalized copy of the given vector.
```lua
local n = Vector.normalized(Vector.xy(10, 0))  -- Vector.xy(1, 0)
```


## Static Functions

### `distance`

{/* distance: (a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
distance(a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the distance between the two vectors.
```lua
local d = Vector.distance(Vector.xy(3, 4), Vector.xy(0, 0))  -- 5
```


### `distanceSquared`

{/* distanceSquared: (a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
distanceSquared(a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the squared distance between the two vectors.
```lua
local d2 = Vector.distanceSquared(Vector.xy(3,4), Vector.xy(0,0))  -- 25
```


### `dot`

{/* dot: (a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
dot(a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the dot product of the two vectors.
```lua
local dp = Vector.dot(Vector.xy(1,2), Vector.xy(3,4))  -- 11 (1*3 + 2*4)
```


### `cross`

{/* cross: (a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
cross(a: Vector, b: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the cross product of two vectors (z-component of the 3D cross product).
```lua
local c = Vector.cross(Vector.xy(1, 0), Vector.xy(0, 1))  -- 1
```


### `length`

{/* length: (v: Vector) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
length(v: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the length of the given vector.
```lua
local len = Vector.length(Vector.xy(3, 4))  -- 5
```


### `lengthSquared`

{/* lengthSquared: (v: Vector) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lengthSquared(v: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the squared length of the given vector.
```lua
local len2 = Vector.lengthSquared(Vector.xy(3, 4))  -- 25
```


## Methods

### `length`

{/* function length(self): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
length() -> number
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.length` instead.
</Warning>

Returns the length of the vector.


### `lengthSquared`

{/* function lengthSquared(self): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lengthSquared() -> number
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.lengthSquared` instead.
</Warning>

Returns the squared length of the vector.
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(3, 4)
local len2 = v:lengthSquared()  -- 25
```


### `normalized`

{/* function normalized(self): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
normalized() -> Vector
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.normalized` instead.
</Warning>

Returns a normalized copy of the vector. If the length is zero,
the result is the zero vector.
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(10, 0)
local n = v:normalized()  -- 1 0
```


### `__eq`

{/* function __eq(self, rhs: Vector): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__eq(rhs: Vector) -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the two vectors have equal components.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(1, 2)
local b = Vector.xy(1, 2)
local c = Vector.xy(2, 1)
print(a == b)  -- true
print(a == c)  -- false
```


### `__unm`

{/* function __unm(self): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__unm() -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the negated vector.
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(2, -3)
local neg = -v   -- -2 3
```


### `__add`

{/* function __add(self, rhs: Vector): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__add(rhs: Vector) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the sum of two vectors.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(2, 3)
local b = Vector.xy(-1, 5)
local c = a + b  -- 1 8
```


### `__sub`

{/* function __sub(self, rhs: Vector): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__sub(rhs: Vector) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the difference between two vectors.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(2, 3)
local b = Vector.xy(-1, 5)
local c = a - b  -- 3 -2
```


### `__mul`

{/* function __mul(self, rhs: number): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__mul(rhs: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the vector scaled by the given number.
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(3, -2)
local doubled = v * 2    -- 6 -4
```


### `__div`

{/* function __div(self, rhs: number): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__div(rhs: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Returns the vector divided by the given number.
```lua
local v = Vector.xy(6, -4)
local half = v / 2    -- 3 -2
```


### `distance`

{/* function distance(self, other: Vector): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
distance(other: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.distance` instead.
</Warning>

Returns the distance to the other vector.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(0, 0)
local b = Vector.xy(3, 4)
print(a:distance(b))  -- 5
```


### `distanceSquared`

{/* function distanceSquared(self, other: Vector): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
distanceSquared(other: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.distanceSquared` instead.
</Warning>

Returns the squared distance to the other vector.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(0, 0)
local b = Vector.xy(3, 4)
print(a:distanceSquared(b))  -- 25
```


### `dot`

{/* function dot(self, other: Vector): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
dot(other: Vector) -> number
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.dot` instead.
</Warning>

Returns the dot product of the vector and the other vector.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(1, 2)
local b = Vector.xy(3, 4)
print(a:dot(b))  -- 11  (1*3 + 2*4)
```


### `lerp`

{/* function lerp(self, other: Vector, t:number): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lerp(other: Vector, t: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

<Warning>
  **Deprecated** - Use `Vector.lerp` instead.
</Warning>

Returns the linear interpolation between the vector and the other
vector, using t where 0 returns the vector and 1 returns the other.
```lua
local a = Vector.xy(0, 0)
local b = Vector.xy(10, 0)
local p = a:lerp(b, 0.5)  -- 5 0
```


### `writeToBuffer`

{/* function writeToBuffer(self, buf: buffer, byteOffset: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
writeToBuffer(buf: buffer, byteOffset: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Writes x, y, z as 12 bytes (three float32) into the buffer at
`byteOffset`.
```lua
local buf = buffer.create(12)
Vector.xyz(1, 2, 3):writeToBuffer(buf, 0)
```


### `writeVec4`

{/* function writeVec4(self, buf: buffer, byteOffset: number, w: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
writeVec4(buf: buffer, byteOffset: number, w: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Writes x, y, z, w as 16 bytes (four float32) into the buffer at
`byteOffset`, matching a vec4 uniform-buffer slot.
```lua
local ubo = buffer.create(16)
lightDir:writeVec4(ubo, 0, 0)  -- w = 0 for a direction
```

==================================================
---
title: Color
---

## Constructors

### `lerp`

{/* lerp: (from: Color, to: Color, t:number) -> Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lerp(from: Color, to: Color, t: number) -> Color
```
</div>

Linearly interpolates between two colors using the parameter t, where
t = 0 returns 'from' and t = 1 returns 'to'.
```lua highlight={7}
local black = Color.rgb(0, 0, 0)
local white = Color.rgb(255, 255, 255)

local t = 0.5

-- Linearly interpolate halfway between black and white
local gray = Color.lerp(black, white, t)

print(gray)
-- Returns a gray color between black and white
```


### `rgb`

{/* rgb: (r: number, g:number, b:number) -> Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
rgb(r: number, g: number, b: number) -> Color
```
</div>

Returns a color constructed from red, green, and blue channels. Alpha
defaults to 255 (fully opaque). Only the low 8 bits of each channel are
kept, so 300 becomes 44 and -1 becomes 255.
```lua
-- Red
self.color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0)
```


### `rgba`

{/* rgba: (r: number, g:number, b:number, a:number) -> Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
rgba(r: number, g: number, b: number, a: number) -> Color
```
</div>

Returns a color constructed from red, green, blue, and alpha channels.
Only the low 8 bits of each channel are kept, so 300 becomes 44 and -1
becomes 255.
```lua
-- Red at 50% opacity
self.color = Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 128)
```


## Static Functions

### `red`

{/* red: (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
red(color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color
```
</div>

Returns the red channel of the color. If a value is
provided, returns a new color with that channel updated.
```lua highlight={2,6}
local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
local redChannel = Color.red(myColor)
print(redChannel)
-- 128

local newColor = Color.red(myColor, 200)
print(Color.red(newColor))
-- 200
```


### `green`

{/* green: (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
green(color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color
```
</div>

Returns the green channel of the color. If a value is
provided, returns a new color with that channel updated.
```lua highlight={2,6}
local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
local greenChannel = Color.green(myColor)
print(greenChannel)
-- 55

local newColor = Color.green(myColor, 200)
print(Color.green(newColor))
-- 200
```


### `blue`

{/* blue: (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
blue(color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color
```
</div>

Returns the blue channel of the color. If a value is
provided, returns a new color with that channel updated.
```lua highlight={2,6}
local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
local blueChannel = Color.blue(myColor)
print(blueChannel)
-- 12

local newColor = Color.blue(myColor, 200)
print(Color.blue(newColor))
-- 200
```


### `alpha`

{/* alpha: (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
alpha(color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color
```
</div>

Returns the alpha channel of the color, or returns a new color with the
alpha channel set to the specified value. Only the low 8 bits of the
value are kept.
```lua highlight={2,6}
local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
local alphaChannel = Color.alpha(myColor)
print(alphaChannel)
-- 128

local newColor = Color.alpha(myColor, 200)
print(Color.alpha(newColor))
-- 200
```


### `opacity`

{/* opacity: (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
opacity(color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color
```
</div>

Returns the opacity of the color as a normalized value in the range
[0.0, 1.0], or returns a new color with its alpha set from the specified
opacity.
```lua highlight={4,9}
local myColor = Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 128)

-- Get the opacity of a color
local myOpacity = Color.opacity(myColor)
print(myOpacity)
-- 0.502

-- Get a new color with the specified opacity
local newColor = Color.opacity(myColor, 1.0)
print(Color.opacity(newColor))
-- 1.0
```


### `toFloat`

{/* toFloat: (color: Color) -> { number } */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
toFloat(color: Color) -> {number}
```
</div>

Convert a Color (ARGB packed integer) to an `{r, g, b, a}` table
with values in 0–1 range. Use with `clearColor` in render passes.
```lua
local cc = Color.toFloat(Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 128))
-- cc = {1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.502}
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/renderer/renderer.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Renderer
---

Provides functions for drawing paths and images, managing clipping, and
applying transforms during rendering.


## Methods

### `drawPath`

{/* function drawPath(self, path: Path, paint: Paint): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
drawPath(path: Path, paint: Paint) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws the given [Path](/scripting/api-reference/path/path) using the specified [Paint](/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint).

For a more detailed explanation and working examples, see [Drawing with Node Scripts](/scripting/protocols/node-scripts#drawing).
```lua
function draw(self: Rectangle, renderer: Renderer)
  renderer:drawPath(self.path, self.paint)
end
```


### `drawImage`

{/* function drawImage(self, image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler,  blendMode: BlendMode, opacity: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
drawImage(image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler, blendMode: BlendMode, opacity: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws an [Image](/scripting/api-reference/image/image) using the [ImageSampler](/scripting/api-reference/image/image-sampler), [BlendMode](/scripting/api-reference/paint/blend-mode), and opacity.

Check out [Scripting demos](/scripting/demos) to see a working example.

```lua highlight={15}
type DrawImage = {
  myImage: Image?,
  sampler: ImageSampler?,
}

function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
  self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
  self.sampler = ImageSampler('clamp', 'clamp', 'bilinear')

  return true
end

function draw(self: DrawImage, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler then
    renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
  end
end

return function(): Node<DrawImage>
  return {
    myImage = nil,
    sampler = nil,
    init = init,
    draw = draw,
  }
end
```


### `drawImageMesh`

{/* function drawImageMesh(self, image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler, vertices: VertexBuffer, uvs: VertexBuffer, triangles: TriangleBuffer, blendMode: BlendMode, opacity: number ): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
drawImageMesh(image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler, vertices: VertexBuffer, uvs: VertexBuffer, triangles: TriangleBuffer, blendMode: BlendMode, opacity: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws an image using mesh data defined by vertices, texture
coordinates, and triangle indices.

Check out [Scripting demos](/scripting/demos) to see a working example.
```lua
function draw(self: DrawImageMesh, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler and self.vertices and self.uvs and self.triangles then
    renderer:drawImageMesh(
      self.myImage,
      self.sampler,
      self.vertices,
      self.uvs,
      self.triangles,
      'srcOver',
      1
    )
  end
end
```


### `drawImageMeshInstanced`

{/* function drawImageMeshInstanced(self, image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler, vertices: VertexBuffer, uvs: VertexBuffer, triangles: TriangleBuffer, instances: MeshInstances): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
drawImageMeshInstanced(image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler, vertices: VertexBuffer, uvs: VertexBuffer, triangles: TriangleBuffer, instances: MeshInstances) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws one mesh once per entry of a [MeshInstances](/scripting/api-reference/mesh/mesh-instances), in a single call.
The blend mode is always `srcOver`. Opacity and the UV transform come
from each instance.
```lua
function draw(self: DrawImageMeshInstanced, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler and self.vertices and self.uvs and self.triangles and self.instances then
    renderer:drawImageMeshInstanced(
      self.myImage,
      self.sampler,
      self.vertices,
      self.uvs,
      self.triangles,
      self.instances
    )
  end
end
```


### `clipPath`

{/* function clipPath(self, path: Path): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
clipPath(path: Path) -> ()
```
</div>

Restricts subsequent drawing to the area defined by the given [Path](/scripting/api-reference/path/path).
Clipping remains in effect until the next restore call.

Check out [Scripting demos](/scripting/demos) to see a working example.
```lua highlight={10}
function draw(self: DrawImageClipped, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler then
    local w: number = self.myImage.width
    local h: number = self.myImage.height
    local rx: number = (w / 2) * self.clipRadiusX
    local ry: number = (h / 2) * self.clipRadiusY
    buildOvalPath(self.clipPath, w / 2, h / 2, rx, ry)

    renderer:save()
    renderer:clipPath(self.clipPath)
    renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end
```


### `save`

{/* function save(self): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
save() -> ()
```
</div>

Saves the current rendering state, including transforms and clipping.
```lua highlight={4}
function draw(self: MyGame, renderer: Renderer)
  -- draw each enemy
  for _, enemy in self.enemies do
    renderer:save()
    enemy.artboard:draw(renderer)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end
```


### `restore`

{/* function restore(self): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
restore() -> ()
```
</div>

Restores the most recently saved rendering state.
```lua highlight={6}
function draw(self: MyGame, renderer: Renderer)
  -- draw each enemy
  for _, enemy in self.enemies do
    renderer:save()
    enemy.artboard:draw(renderer)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end
```


### `transform`

{/* function transform(self, transform: Mat2D): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
transform(transform: Mat2D) -> ()
```
</div>

Applies a transform to the current rendering state. Transforms are
applied cumulatively until restored.
```lua highlight={7}
function draw(self: TransformedImage, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler then
    local m = Mat2D.withScale(2, 3)
    -- Adjust matrix terms directly for additional skew/stretch control.
    m.xx = 5

    renderer:save()
    renderer:transform(m)
    renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end
```


### `modulateOpacity`

{/* function modulateOpacity(self, opacity: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
modulateOpacity(opacity: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Multiplies the opacity of subsequent draw calls by `opacity` (0..1).
Stacks multiplicatively and is captured by save()/restore(), so the
common pattern is: renderer:save(); renderer:modulateOpacity(a);
... draw ...; renderer:restore().


### `modulateColor`

{/* function modulateColor(self, color: Color): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
modulateColor(color: Color) -> ()
```
</div>

Multiplies `color` into subsequent draw calls, channel by channel.
Stacks and is captured by save()/restore() like modulateOpacity.


### `setColorModulation`

{/* function setColorModulation(self, color: Color): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
setColorModulation(color: Color) -> ()
```
</div>

Sets the modulation color outright rather than multiplying, which
lets an inner scope undo an outer one: draw an artboard under black,
then set the color for the drawables that should keep their paint.
Captured by save()/restore(); inside a draw visitor it ends with the
visit, so the visitor needs no save()/restore() of its own.

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/mat4/mat4.mdx

---
title: Mat4
---

Represents a 4x4 column-major transformation matrix, suitable for 3D
transforms and direct upload to a GPU uniform buffer.
```lua
-- Construct an MVP matrix
local proj = Mat4.perspective(math.rad(60), 16 / 9, 0.1, 100)
local view = Mat4.fromTranslation(0, 0, -3) -- camera 3 units back
local model = Mat4.fromRotationY(angle)
local mvp = proj * view * model

-- Upload to a uniform buffer (64 bytes, column-major)
mvp:writeToBuffer(uboBytes, 0)
```


## Fields

### `m11`

Element at row R, column C (1-indexed). For example `m.m12` is the
entry in row 1, column 2.
```lua
local m = Mat4.identity()
m.m11 = 2 -- scale x
m.m22 = 3 -- scale y
m.m14 = 50 -- translate x
```


### `m12`

### `m13`

### `m14`

### `m21`

### `m22`

### `m23`

### `m24`

### `m31`

### `m32`

### `m33`

### `m34`

### `m41`

### `m42`

### `m43`

### `m44`

## Constructors

### `identity`

{/* identity: () -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
identity() -> Mat4
```
</div>

Returns the 4x4 identity matrix.


### `values`

{/* values: (
        c0x: number, c0y: number, c0z: number, c0w: number,
        c1x: number, c1y: number, c1z: number, c1w: number,
        c2x: number, c2y: number, c2z: number, c2w: number,
        c3x: number, c3y: number, c3z: number, c3w: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
values(c0x: number, c0y: number, c0z: number, c0w: number, c1x: number, c1y: number, c1z: number, c1w: number, c2x: number, c2y: number, c2z: number, c2w: number, c3x: number, c3y: number, c3z: number, c3w: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a matrix from 16 components, supplied column-major (column 0
first: c0x, c0y, c0z, c0w, c1x, ...).


### `fromTranslation`

{/* fromTranslation: (x: number, y: number, z: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
fromTranslation(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a translation matrix.
```lua
local t = Mat4.fromTranslation(10, 20, 30)
```


### `fromScale`

{/* fromScale: (x: number, y: number?, z: number?) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
fromScale(x: number, y: number?, z: number?) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a scale matrix. If `y` and `z` are omitted, uniform scaling
by `x` is applied to all axes.
```lua
local s1 = Mat4.fromScale(2)        -- uniform 2x
local s2 = Mat4.fromScale(1, 2, 1)  -- 2x in Y only
```


### `fromRotationX`

{/* fromRotationX: (radians: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
fromRotationX(radians: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a rotation matrix around the X axis (radians).


### `fromRotationY`

{/* fromRotationY: (radians: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
fromRotationY(radians: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a rotation matrix around the Y axis (radians).


### `fromRotationZ`

{/* fromRotationZ: (radians: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
fromRotationZ(radians: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a rotation matrix around the Z axis (radians).


### `perspective`

{/* perspective: (fovY: number, aspect: number, near: number, far: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
perspective(fovY: number, aspect: number, near: number, far: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a right-handed perspective projection matrix that maps z to
the [0, 1] NDC depth range. `fovY` is in radians; `near` and `far`
are positive distances.
```lua
local proj = Mat4.perspective(math.rad(60), 16 / 9, 0.1, 100)
```


### `perspectiveReverseZ`

{/* perspectiveReverseZ: (fovY: number, aspect: number, near: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
perspectiveReverseZ(fovY: number, aspect: number, near: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Right-handed perspective with reverse-Z (near -> 1, far -> 0) and an
infinite far plane. Combined with a float depth buffer this gives a
near-uniform 1/z depth distribution across the entire frustum — the
best precision an arbitrary scene can achieve. The depth buffer must
be cleared to 0 (not 1) and the depth test flipped to GREATER.
```lua
local proj = Mat4.perspectiveReverseZ(math.rad(60), 16 / 9, 0.1)
```


### `lookAt`

{/* lookAt: (eye: Vector, center: Vector, up: Vector) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lookAt(eye: Vector, center: Vector, up: Vector) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a right-handed view matrix looking from `eye` toward
`center` (GLM convention). `up` need not be normalized.
```lua
local view = Mat4.lookAt(Vector.xyz(0, 2, 5), Vector.origin(), Vector.xyz(0, 1, 0))
```


### `ortho`

{/* ortho: (left: number, right: number, bottom: number, top: number, near: number, far: number) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
ortho(left: number, right: number, bottom: number, top: number, near: number, far: number) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Creates a right-handed orthographic projection matrix that maps z to
the [0, 1] NDC depth range (matching `Mat4.perspective`), e.g. for
shadow-map cascades or 2D overlays.
```lua
local proj = Mat4.ortho(-10, 10, -10, 10, 0.1, 100)
```


### `multiply`

{/* multiply: (output: Mat4, a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
multiply(output: Mat4, a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Writes `a * b` into `output`, reusing its storage. Returns `output`.
Use this in tight loops to avoid allocating a new [Mat4](/scripting/api-reference/mat4/mat4) per
multiplication. `output` may alias `a` or `b`.
```lua
local out = Mat4.identity()
for i = 1, 1000 do Mat4.multiply(out, view, model) end
```


### `multiplyAffine`

{/* multiplyAffine: (output: Mat4, a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
multiplyAffine(output: Mat4, a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Like `Mat4.multiply`, but assumes both inputs are affine (bottom row
[0, 0, 0, 1] — any composition of translation/scale/rotation matrices
qualifies). Skips the bottom-row work for ~25% fewer FLOPs per
multiplication. The result is always affine. Caller must ensure both
inputs are affine; passing a non-affine input gives an incorrect
result.
```lua highlight={3}
local world = Mat4.identity()
for _, bone in ipairs(bones) do
    Mat4.multiplyAffine(world, parent, bone.local)
end
```


## Static Functions

### `invert`

{/* invert: (output: Mat4, input: Mat4) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
invert(output: Mat4, input: Mat4) -> boolean
```
</div>

Writes the inverse of `input` into `output`, returning true on
success or false if `input` is singular.
```lua
local inv = Mat4.identity()
local ok = Mat4.invert(inv, m)
```


### `invertAffine`

{/* invertAffine: (output: Mat4, input: Mat4) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
invertAffine(output: Mat4, input: Mat4) -> boolean
```
</div>

Writes the affine inverse of `input` into `output`. See
`Mat4:invertAffine` for the contract; faster than `Mat4.invert`.


## Methods

### `invert`

{/* function invert(self): Mat4? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
invert() -> Mat4?
```
</div>

Linear column-major access. Indices 1..4 are column 0, 5..8 are
column 1, 9..12 are column 2, 13..16 are column 3 (translation).
```lua
local m = Mat4.identity()
m[13] = 50 -- translate x
m[14] = 100 -- translate y
m[15] = 25 -- translate z
```
Returns the inverse of the matrix, or `nil` if the matrix is singular.
```lua highlight={2}
local m = Mat4.fromTranslation(50, 100, 25)
local inv = m:invert()
```


### `transpose`

{/* function transpose(self): Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
transpose() -> Mat4
```
</div>

Returns the transpose of the matrix.
```lua highlight={2}
local m = Mat4.fromRotationY(math.rad(45))
local t = m:transpose()
```


### `transformPoint`

{/* function transformPoint(self, x: number, y: number, z: number): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
transformPoint(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> Vector
```
</div>

Transforms the given 3D point by the matrix (treating w = 1) and
returns the result as a [Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector). If the homogeneous w of the result
is non-unit (e.g. after a perspective matrix), the returned point is
divided through.
```lua highlight={3}
local m = Mat4.fromTranslation(10, 20, 30)
local p = m:transformPoint(1, 2, 3)
print(p.x, p.y, p.z) -- 11, 22, 33
```


### `transformVec4`

{/* function transformVec4(
        self, x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number): (number, number, number, number) */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
transformVec4(x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number) -> (number, number, number, number)
```
</div>

Transforms the given homogeneous 4D vector by the matrix and returns
the four components as multiple values, without perspective divide.
Use this when the caller needs to inspect or carry the homogeneous
`w` (e.g. clip-space coordinates).
```lua highlight={2}
local mvp = proj * view * model
local x, y, z, w = mvp:transformVec4(px, py, pz, 1)
```


### `writeToBuffer`

{/* function writeToBuffer(self, buf: buffer, byteOffset: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
writeToBuffer(buf: buffer, byteOffset: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Writes the matrix as 64 bytes (column-major, 16 float32 entries) into
the given buffer at `byteOffset`. The buffer must have at least 64
bytes available from the offset.
```lua highlight={3}
local mvp = Mat4.identity()
local ubo = buffer.create(64)
mvp:writeToBuffer(ubo, 0)
```


### `__eq`

{/* function __eq(self, rhs: Mat4): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__eq(rhs: Mat4) -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if all 16 components of the two matrices are equal.


### `__mul`

{/* function __mul(self, rhs: Mat4): Mat4 */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__mul(rhs: Mat4) -> Mat4
```
</div>

Returns the matrix product of two matrices. Useful for composing
transforms, e.g. `proj * view * model`. Allocates a new [Mat4](/scripting/api-reference/mat4/mat4); in
tight loops prefer `Mat4.multiply(out, a, b)` to reuse storage.


### `invertAffine`

{/* function invertAffine(self): Mat4? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
invertAffine() -> Mat4?
```
</div>

Closed-form inverse for affine matrices (bottom row [0, 0, 0, 1] —
any composition of `fromTranslation`/`fromScale`/`fromRotationX/Y/Z`
qualifies). Returns nil if the linear part is singular. Faster than
`:invert()` and avoids the full 4x4 cofactor work.
```lua highlight={2}
local m = Mat4.fromTranslation(3, -4, 5) * Mat4.fromRotationY(0.4)
local inv = m:invertAffine()
```

---
title: DataValue
---

Base type for values that can be stored in inputs. Provides
functions for checking the underlying value type.


## Static Functions

### `number`

{/* number: () -> DataValueNumber */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
number() -> DataValueNumber
```
</div>

Creates a [DataValueNumber](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/data-value-number) that stores a number.
```lua
local data = DataValue.number()
data.value = 42

print(data.value) -- 42
```


### `string`

{/* string: () -> DataValueString */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
string() -> DataValueString
```
</div>

Creates a [DataValueString](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/data-value-string) that stores a string.
```lua
local data = DataValue.string()
data.value = 'Rive for life!'

print(data.value) -- Rive for life!
```


### `boolean`

{/* boolean: () -> DataValueBoolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
boolean() -> DataValueBoolean
```
</div>

Creates a [DataValueBoolean](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/data-value-boolean) that stores a boolean.
```lua
local data = DataValue.boolean()
data.value = false

print(data.value) -- false
```


### `color`

{/* color: () -> DataValueColor */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
color() -> DataValueColor
```
</div>

Creates a [DataValueColor](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/data-value-color) that stores a [Color](/scripting/api-reference/color/color).
```lua
local data = DataValue.color()
data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)

print(Color.red(data.value)) -- 255
```


## Methods

### `isNumber`

{/* function isNumber(self): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isNumber() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the value is a number.
```lua
local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
print(dv.isNumber) -- true
```


### `isString`

{/* function isString(self): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isString() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the value is a string.
```lua
local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
print(dv.isString) -- false
```


### `isBoolean`

{/* function isBoolean(self): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isBoolean() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the value is a boolean.
```lua
local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
print(dv.isBoolean) -- false
```


### `isColor`

{/* function isColor(self): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isColor() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the value is a color.
```lua
local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
print(dv.isColor) -- false
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/data-value/property-trigger.mdx
==================================================
---
title: PropertyTrigger
---

Represents a trigger property that can fire events and notify listeners.
Unlike other [Property](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/property) types, a trigger does not store a persistent value. It emits an event when fire() is called.


## Fields

### `addListener`

Registers a listener that is invoked when the trigger fires.

This function has two signatures:
- `addListener(callback)` — Simple form, just pass the callback function.
- `addListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor object and a callback.
The anchor is stored alongside the listener and passed to the callback
when invoked. This is useful for preventing garbage collection of objects
you need to keep alive while the listener is active.

**Important:** If you obtain a ViewModel or property using a local variable
(e.g., `local vm = context:viewModel()`) and add listeners without storing
the ViewModel elsewhere, it may be garbage collected after the function
returns. To prevent this, either:
- Store the ViewModel on `self` (e.g., `self.vm = context:viewModel()`)
- Pass the ViewModel as the anchor parameter to `addListener`

```lua highlight={5}
local vmi = context:viewModel()
if vmi then
  local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
  if cannon then
    cannon:addListener(function()
      print("cannon fired!")
    end)

    cannon:fire()
  end
end
```

Using the anchor parameter to keep the ViewModel alive:
```lua highlight={5}
local vm = context:viewModel()
if vm then
  local cannon = vm:getTrigger('cannon')
  if cannon then
    cannon:addListener(vm, function(anchor)
      -- 'anchor' is the vm we passed, kept alive by the listener
      print("cannon fired!")
    end)
  end
end
```


### `removeListener`

Removes a previously registered listener.
Always remove listeners when they are no longer needed to avoid leaks.

This function has two signatures:
- `removeListener(callback)` — Pass the callback function to remove.
- `removeListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor and the callback.
The anchor parameter is accepted for API symmetry with `addListener`,
but only the callback is used for matching.

```lua highlight={17}
function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
  local vmi = context:viewModel()
  if vmi then
    local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    if cannon then
      self.cannon = cannon
      self.onCannonFired = onCannonFired
      cannon:addListener(onCannonFired)
    end
  end

  return true
end

function removeCannonListener(self: MyNode)
  if self.cannon then
    self.cannon:removeListener(self.onCannonFired)
  end
end
```


## Methods

### `fire`

{/* fire: (self:PropertyTrigger) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
fire() -> ()
```
</div>

Fires the trigger and notifies all registered listeners.
```lua highlight={9}
local vmi = context:viewModel()
if vmi then
  local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
  if cannon then
    cannon:addListener(function()
      print("cannon fired!")
    end)

    cannon:fire()
  end
end
```

---
title: DataValueColor
---

[DataValue](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/data-value) that stores a color value encoded as a number, with
red, green, blue, and alpha components.


## Fields

### `value`

The full color value encoded as a number.
```lua
local dv: DataValueColor = DataValue.color()
dv.value = Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 155)
```


### `red`

Color components in the range [0, 255].
```lua highlight={4,5}
local data = DataValue.color()
data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)

print(data.red) -- 128
data.red = 233
```


### `green`

Color components in the range [0, 255].
```lua highlight={4,5}
local data = DataValue.color()
data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)

print(data.green) -- 55
data.green = 233
```


### `blue`

Color components in the range [0, 255].
```lua highlight={4,5}
local data = DataValue.color()
data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)

print(data.blue) -- 12
data.blue = 233
```


### `alpha`

Alpha component in the range [0, 255].
```lua highlight={4,5}
local data = DataValue.color()
data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)

print(data.alpha) -- 1
data.alpha = 255
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/data-value/listener.mdx

---
title: Listener
---

Represents a listener callback that can observe changes on an object.
See [Property addListener](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/property#addlistener) and [PropertyTrigger addListener](/scripting/api-reference/data-value/property-trigger#addlistener).




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/data-value/property.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Property
---

Represents a mutable property that stores a value and supports change listeners.


## Fields

### `value`

The current value of the property.

You can both read and assign to this field.
```lua highlight={4,5}
local health = vm:getNumber("health")

if health then
  print(health.value) -- read
  health.value = 100  -- write
end
```


### `addListener`

Registers a listener that is called whenever the property's value changes.

This function has two signatures:
- `addListener(callback)` — Simple form, just pass the callback function.
- `addListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor object and a callback.
The anchor is stored alongside the listener and passed to the callback
when invoked. This is useful for preventing garbage collection of objects
you need to keep alive while the listener is active.

**Important:** If you obtain a ViewModel or property using a local variable
(e.g., `local vm = context:viewModel()`) and add listeners without storing
the ViewModel elsewhere, it may be garbage collected after the function
returns. To prevent this, either:
- Store the ViewModel on `self` (e.g., `self.vm = context:viewModel()`)
- Pass the ViewModel as the anchor parameter to `addListener`

```lua highlight={8,10}
local health = vm:getNumber("health")

if health then
  local function onHealthChanged(prop)
    print("New health:", prop.value)
  end

  health:addListener(onHealthChanged)

  health.value = 50 -- Triggers listener
end
```

Using the anchor parameter to keep the ViewModel alive:
```lua highlight={5}
local vm = context:viewModel()
local health = vm:getNumber("health")

if health then
  health:addListener(vm, function(anchor)
    -- 'anchor' is the vm we passed, kept alive by the listener
    print("Health changed!")
  end)
end
```


### `removeListener`

Removes a previously registered listener.

This function has two signatures:
- `removeListener(callback)` — Pass the callback function to remove.
- `removeListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor and the callback.
The anchor parameter is accepted for API symmetry with `addListener`,
but only the callback is used for matching.

```lua highlight={6}
local health = vm:getNumber("health")

if health then
  local function onHealthChanged(prop)
    print("New health:", prop.value)
    health:removeListener(onHealthChanged)
  end

  health:addListener(onHealthChanged)

  health.value = 50 -- Triggers listener
end
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/mat2d/mat2d.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Mat2D
---

Represents a 2D transformation matrix with components for scaling,
rotation, shear, and translation.
```lua
-- Construct a matrix manually
local m = Mat2D.identity()

m.xx = 2    -- scale x
m.yy = 3    -- scale y
m.tx = 50   -- translate x
m.ty = 100  -- translate y

local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 20)

-- (10,20) → (20,60) → (70,160)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 70, 160
```


## Fields

### `xx`

The xx component of the matrix.
```lua highlight={4}
local m = Mat2D.identity()

-- Double horizontal scale
m.xx = 2

local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 5)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 20, 5
```


### `xy`

The xy component of the matrix, the vertical skew.
```lua highlight={4}
local m = Mat2D.identity()

-- Add vertical skew
m.xy = 1

local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 5)
-- y = 5 + (1 * 10)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 10, 15
```


### `yx`

The yx component of the matrix, the horizontal skew.
```lua highlight={4}
local m = Mat2D.identity()

-- Add horizontal skew
m.yx = 1

local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 5)
-- x = 10 + (1 * 5)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 15, 5
```


### `yy`

The yy component of the matrix.
```lua highlight={4}
local m = Mat2D.identity()

-- Triple vertical scale
m.yy = 3

local r = m * Vector.xy(4, 5)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 4, 15
```


### `tx`

Translation along the x-axis.
```lua highlight={3}
local m = Mat2D.identity()

m.tx = 50

local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 20)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 60, 20
```


### `ty`

Translation along the y-axis.
```lua highlight={3}
local m = Mat2D.identity()

m.ty = 100

local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 20)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 10, 120
```


### `withTranslation`

Creates a translation matrix from the given x and y values or from a
[Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector) position.
```lua highlight={2,6}
-- From numbers
local t1 = Mat2D.withTranslation(50, 100)

-- From a Vector
local pos = Vector.xy(50, 100)
local t2 = Mat2D.withTranslation(pos)
```


### `withScale`

Creates a scale matrix from the given x and y values or from a [Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector).
```lua highlight={2,5,9}
-- Uniform scale (y defaults to x if omitted)
local s1 = Mat2D.withScale(2)

-- Non-uniform scale
local s2 = Mat2D.withScale(2, 3)

-- From a Vector
local scale = Vector.xy(2, 3)
local s3 = Mat2D.withScale(scale)
```


### `withScaleAndTranslation`

Creates a scale-and-translation matrix from numeric values or vectors.
```lua highlight={4,14}
-- Numbers Overloaded

-- Scale by (2, 3) then translate by (50, 100)
local st = Mat2D.withScaleAndTranslation(2, 3, 50, 100)

local p = Vector.xy(10, 20)
local r = st * p

-- (10,20) -> scaled (20,60) -> translated (70,160)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 70, 160

-- Vectors Overloaded

local st = Mat2D.withScaleAndTranslation(
  Vector.xy(2, 3),      -- scale
  Vector.xy(50, 100)    -- position / translation
)

local r = st * Vector.xy(10, 20)
print(r.x, r.y) -- 70, 160
```


## Constructors

### `values`

{/* values: (xx:number, xy:number, yx: number, yy: number, tx: number, ty: number) -> Mat2D */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
values(xx: number, xy: number, yx: number, yy: number, tx: number, ty: number) -> Mat2D
```
</div>

Creates a matrix using the specified components.
```lua
-- xx=1, xy=skewY (vertical skew), yx=skewX (horizontal skew), yy=1, tx=0, ty=0
local newMat = Mat2D.values(1, self.skewY, self.skewX, 1, 0, 0)
```


### `identity`

{/* identity: () -> Mat2D */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
identity() -> Mat2D
```
</div>

Returns the identity matrix.
```lua
-- xx = 1, xy = 0, yx = 0, yy = 1, tx = 0, ty = 0
local newMat = Mat2D.identity()
```


### `withRotation`

{/* withRotation: (radians: number) -> Mat2D */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
withRotation(radians: number) -> Mat2D
```
</div>

Creates a rotation matrix from the given angle in radians.
```lua highlight={1}
local rot = Mat2D.withRotation(math.rad(90))
local r = rot * Vector.xy(1, 0)

print(math.floor(r.x + 0.5), math.floor(r.y + 0.5)) -- 0, 1
```


## Static Functions

### `invert`

{/* invert: (output: Mat2D, input: Mat2D) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
invert(output: Mat2D, input: Mat2D) -> boolean
```
</div>

Writes the inverse of 'input' into 'output'. Returns true if the input
matrix is invertible.
```lua highlight={4}
local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(50, 100)

local inv = Mat2D.identity()
local ok = Mat2D.invert(inv, m)
print(ok) -- true

local p = Vector.xy(10, 20)
local r = inv * (m * p)

-- Applying m then inv returns the original point
print(r.x, r.y) -- 10, 20
```


## Methods

### `invert`

{/* function invert(self): Mat2D? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
invert() -> Mat2D?
```
</div>

Provides indexed access to the matrix components.
```lua
local m = Mat2D.identity()

-- Indices map to: xx, xy, yx, yy, tx, ty
m[1] = 2    -- xx
m[5] = 50   -- tx

print(m[1], m.xx) -- 2, 2
print(m[5], m.tx) -- 50, 50
```
Returns the inverse of the matrix, or nil if the matrix is not invertible.
```lua highlight={2}
local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(50, 100)
local inv = m:invert()

if inv then
  local p = Vector.xy(10, 20)
  local result = inv * (m * p)
  print(result.x, result.y) -- 10, 20
end
```


### `isIdentity`

{/* function isIdentity(self): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isIdentity() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the matrix is the identity transform.
```lua
local newMat = Mat2D.identity()
print(newMat:isIdentity())
```


### `__eq`

{/* function __eq(self, rhs: Mat2D): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__eq(rhs: Mat2D) -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if all components of the two matrices are equal.
```lua highlight={4}
local a = Mat2D.values(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)
local b = Mat2D.identity()

print(a == b) -- true
```


### `__mul`

{/* function __mul(self, rhs: Vector): Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__mul(rhs: Vector) -> Vector
```
</div>

Transforms the given [Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector) by the matrix and returns the result.
```lua highlight={5}
local translation = Mat2D.values(1, 0, 0, 1, 50, 100)
local point = Vector.xy(10, 20)

-- Multiply matrix by vector
local result = translation * point

print(result.x, result.y) -- 60, 120
```


### `__mul`

{/* function __mul(self, rhs: Mat2D): Mat2D */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__mul(rhs: Mat2D) -> Mat2D
```
</div>

Returns the matrix product of this matrix and the given matrix
```lua highlight={5}
local translation = Mat2D.values(1, 0, 0, 1, 50, 100)
local scale = Mat2D.values(2, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0)

-- Combine transforms
local combined = translation * scale

local point = Vector.xy(10, 20)
local result = combined * point

print(result.x, result.y) -- 70, 140
```

---
title: PaintDefinition
---

A partial set of paint properties used to initialize or update a Paint
instance. All fields are optional.


## Fields

### `style`

The painting style (stroke or fill).
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.style = 'fill'
```


### `join`

Stroke join behavior for corners.
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.join = 'round'
```


### `cap`

Stroke cap used for line endings.
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.cap = 'round'
```


### `thickness`

Thickness of the stroked path.
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.thickness = 4
```


### `blendMode`

Blending mode used when compositing.
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.blendMode = 'multiply'
```


### `feather`

Feathering amount.
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.feather = 3
```


### `gradient`

[Gradient](/scripting/api-reference/gradient/gradient) fill applied to the paint.
If explicitly set to `false`, removes any existing gradient.

```lua highlight={7}
local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(10, 0), {
  { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
  { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
})

local paint = Paint.new()
paint.gradient = g
```


### `gradientTransform`

Transform applied to the paint's gradient.
```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.gradientTransform = Mat2D.withTranslation(10, 0)
```


### `color`

Color. See [Color](/scripting/api-reference/color/color).




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Paint
---

Describes how shapes are drawn, including fill or stroke style, thickness,
color, gradient, and blending behavior.


## Fields

### `style`

Painting style of type [PaintStyle](/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint-style).
```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  style = 'stroke',
})
```


### `join`

Stroke join behavior for corners. See [StrokeJoin](/scripting/api-reference/paint/stroke-join).
```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  join = 'round',
  style = 'stroke',
})
```


### `cap`

Stroke cap used for line endings. See [StrokeCap](/scripting/api-reference/paint/stroke-cap).
```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  cap = 'round',
  style = 'stroke',
})
```


### `thickness`

Thickness of the stroked path.
```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  thickness = 4,
  style = 'stroke',
})
```


### `blendMode`

Blending mode used when compositing. See [BlendMode](/scripting/api-reference/paint/blend-mode).
```lua highlight={4}
-- Create a new paint with a color and multiply blend mode
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  blendMode = 'multiply',
  style = 'fill',
})
```


### `feather`

Feathering amount.
```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  feather = 4,
  style = 'stroke',
})
```


### `gradient`

[Gradient](/scripting/api-reference/gradient/gradient) applied to fill (if present).

```lua highlight={8}
local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(10, 0), {
  { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
  { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
})

self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  gradient = g,
  style = 'fill',
})
```


### `gradientTransform`

Transform applied to the paint's `gradient`.

```lua highlight={9}
local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(10, 0), {
  { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
  { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
})

self.paint = Paint.with({
  gradient = g,
  gradientTransform = Mat2D.withTranslation(10, 0),
  style = 'fill',
})
```


### `color`

Color. See [Color](/scripting/api-reference/color/color).
```lua highlight={2}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  style = 'fill',
})
```


## Constructors

### `new`

{/* new: () -> Paint */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
new() -> Paint
```
</div>

Creates a new [Paint](/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint) object with default settings.

```lua
local paint = Paint.new()
paint.style = 'fill'
paint.color = Color.rgb(255, 200, 80)
```


### `with`

{/* with: (values:PaintDefinition) -> Paint */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
with(values: PaintDefinition) -> Paint
```
</div>

Creates a new Paint initialized from the provided [PaintDefinition](/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint-definition).

```lua
local strokePaint = Paint.with({
  style = 'stroke',
  thickness = 3,
  color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 102),
  join = 'round',
  cap = 'round',
})
```


## Methods

### `copy`

{/* function copy(self, values:PaintDefinition?): Paint */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
copy(values: PaintDefinition?) -> Paint
```
</div>

Returns a new Paint that copies this one, optionally overriding selected
properties with values from the provided [PaintDefinition](/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint-definition).
Returns a new [Paint](/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint) instance.

```lua highlight={6,7,8,9}
local base = Paint.with({
  style = 'fill',
  color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0),
})

local outline = base:copy({
  style = 'stroke',
  thickness = 4,
})
```

---
title: BlendMode
---

Defines how the paint’s color or gradient is composited with the content
behind it.

* `srcOver`
* `additive`
* `screen`
* `overlay`
* `darken`
* `lighten`
* `colorDodge`
* `colorBurn`
* `hardLight`
* `softLight`
* `difference`
* `exclusion`
* `multiply`
* `hue`
* `saturation`
* `color`
* `luminosity`

```lua highlight={4}
-- Create a new paint with a color and multiply blend mode
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  blendMode = 'multiply',
  style = 'fill',
})
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/paint/stroke-join.mdx
==================================================
---
title: StrokeJoin
---

Defines how two stroke segments are joined at a corner.
* `miter` — Sharp corner.
* `round` — Rounded corner.
* `bevel` — Flattened corner.

```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  join = 'round',
  style = 'stroke',
})
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/paint/paint-style.mdx
==================================================
---
title: PaintStyle
---

Specifies how the shape should be painted.
* `stroke`
* `fill`

```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  style = 'stroke',
})
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/paint/stroke-cap.mdx
==================================================
---
title: StrokeCap
---

Defines the shape used at the ends of open stroke segments.
* `butt` — Squared end with no extension.
* `round` — Semicircular cap.
* `square` — Squared cap that extends past the end point.

```lua highlight={3}
self.paint = Paint.with({
  color = Color.rgb(255, 100, 50),
  cap = 'round',
  style = 'stroke',
})
```
