TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/path/contour-measure.mdx
==================================================
---
title: ContourMeasure
---

A ContourMeasure is a way to measure and manipulate a single contour within a path.
A contour is one continuous drawing sequence that starts with a `moveTo` and continues until the next `moveTo` (or the end of the path).


## Fields

### `next`

Returns the next [ContourMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/contour-measure) in the path, or nil if this is the last
contour. Use this to iterate through all contours in a path after calling
path:contours(). Each read advances through the path, so read it once
per contour.
```lua
local contour = pathData:contours()
while contour do
  print(contour.length)
  contour = contour.next
end
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/path/path-command.mdx
==================================================
---
title: PathCommand
---

A PathCommand represents a single drawing instruction inside a Path.
Each command has a type, and a variable number of points depending on that type.


## Fields

### `type`

```lua highlight={5}
local path = Path.new()
path:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
path:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 0))

for i, command in ipairs(path) do
  print(i, command.type)
end
-- 1 moveTo
-- 2 lineTo
```
See [CommandType](/scripting/api-reference/path/command-type).


## Methods

### `__len`

{/* function __len(self): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__len() -> number
```
</div>

The number of points varies depending on the command type:
- `moveTo`: 1 point
- `lineTo`: 1 point
- `quadTo`: 2 points
- `cubicTo`: 3 points
- `close`: 0 points
```lua highlight={11}
local path = Path.new()
path:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
path:cubicTo(
  Vector.xy(25, -40),
  Vector.xy(75, 40),
  Vector.xy(100, 0)
)

local command = path[2]
print(command.type)      -- cubicTo
print(#command)          -- 3
```
Returns the number of points stored on this command.
```lua
local count = #command
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/path/path.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Path
---

Path is a mutable path object that can be drawn by a Renderer. An unchanged
path can be drawn multiple times per frame. However, if you mutate it (via
moveTo, lineTo, cubicTo, add, etc.) after drawing, you must wait until the
next frame to draw it again.


## Constructors

### `new`

{/* new: () -> Path */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
new() -> Path
```
</div>

```lua highlight={2}
local path = Path.new()
path:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
```


## Methods

### `moveTo`

{/* moveTo: (self: Path, to: Vector) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
moveTo(to: Vector) -> ()
```
</div>

Moves the current point to the specified location, starting a new contour.
```lua
path:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
```


### `lineTo`

{/* lineTo: (self: Path, to: Vector) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lineTo(to: Vector) -> ()
```
</div>

Adds a straight line segment from the current point to the specified point.
```lua
path:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 0))
```


### `quadTo`

{/* quadTo: (self: Path, control: Vector, to: Vector) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
quadTo(control: Vector, to: Vector) -> ()
```
</div>

Adds a quadratic Bézier curve from the current point to the specified point,
using the control point to define the curve shape.
```lua
path:quadTo(
  Vector.xy(-50, -50), -- control point
  Vector.xy(0, 0)      -- end point
)
```


### `cubicTo`

{/* cubicTo: (self: Path, controlOut: Vector, controlIn: Vector, to: Vector) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
cubicTo(controlOut: Vector, controlIn: Vector, to: Vector) -> ()
```
</div>

Adds a cubic Bézier curve from the current point to the specified point,
using `controlOut` for the start tangent and `controlIn` for the end tangent.
```lua
path:cubicTo(
  Vector.xy(25, -40),  -- control point out
  Vector.xy(75, 40),   -- control point in
  Vector.xy(100, 0)    -- end point
)
```


### `close`

{/* close: (self: Path) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
close() -> ()
```
</div>

Closes the current contour by adding a line segment from the current point
back to the first point of the contour (the last `moveTo`).
```lua
-- Draw a rectangle
path:moveTo(Vector.xy(-10, -10))
path:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, -10))
path:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 10))
path:lineTo(Vector.xy(-10, 10))
-- Close the path
path:close()
```


### `__len`

{/* function __len(self): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__len() -> number
```
</div>

Each entry is a [PathCommand](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-command) describing one segment or action in the path.
```lua
local cmd = path[1]
print(cmd.type)
```
Returns the number of commands in the path.
```lua
local count = #path
print(count)
```


### `reset`

{/* reset: (self: Path) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
reset() -> ()
```
</div>

Do not mutate or reset a [Path](/scripting/api-reference/path/path) in the same frame after drawing it.
If you need to change it, wait until the next frame.
Only call `reset` on subsequent frames if you've called `Renderer.drawPath`
with it.
```lua
path:reset()
```


### `add`

{/* add: (self: Path, other: PathData, transform: Mat2D?) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
add(other: PathData, transform: Mat2D?) -> ()
```
</div>

Appends the commands from `other` onto this path. If `transform` is provided,
the appended commands are transformed as they are added.
```lua
local dst = Path.new()
local src = Path.new()

src:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
src:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 0))
src:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 10))
src:close()

-- Add `src` into `dst` (optionally with a transform)
dst:add(src)
```


### `contours`

{/* contours: (self: Path) -> ContourMeasure? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
contours() -> ContourMeasure?
```
</div>

Returns a [ContourMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/contour-measure) for the first contour in the path. A contour is a
sequence of path segments starting at a `moveTo` and ending before the next
`moveTo` (or end of path). Use the `next` property on the returned
[ContourMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/contour-measure) to iterate through subsequent contours. Returns `nil` if the
path has no contours.
```lua
local contour = path:contours()
while contour do
  print(contour.length)
  contour = contour.next
end
```


### `measure`

{/* measure: (self: Path) -> PathMeasure */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
measure() -> PathMeasure
```
</div>

Returns a [PathMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-measure) that measures the entire path across all contours.
This provides the total length and allows operations on the path as a whole.
```lua
local measure = path:measure()
local pathLength = measure.length
print(pathLength)
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/path/path-measure.mdx
==================================================
---
title: PathMeasure
---

## Fields

### `length`

The total length of the path across all contours.
```lua highlight={11}
local function buildPath(path: Path)
    path:reset()
    path:moveTo(Vector.xy(-150, 0))
    path:cubicTo(Vector.xy(-80, -120), Vector.xy(80, 120), Vector.xy(150, 0))
    path:close()
    end

    function init(self: PathMeasureDemo, _context: Context): boolean
    buildPath(self.path)

    local measure = self.path:measure()
    print('length:', measure.length)

    return true
end
```


### `isClosed`

Returns true only if the path has exactly one contour and that contour is
closed. Paths with multiple contours always return false, even if all
contours are closed.
```lua highlight={11}
local function buildPath(path: Path)
    path:reset()
    path:moveTo(Vector.xy(-150, 0))
    path:cubicTo(Vector.xy(-80, -120), Vector.xy(80, 120), Vector.xy(150, 0))
    end

    function init(self: PathMeasureDemo, _context: Context): boolean
    buildPath(self.path)

    local measure = self.path:measure()
    print('isClosed:', measure.isClosed)

    return true
end
```


## Methods

### `positionAndTangent`

{/* positionAndTangent: (self: PathMeasure, distance: number) -> (Vector, Vector) */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
positionAndTangent(distance: number) -> (Vector, Vector)
```
</div>

Returns the position and tangent vector at the given distance along the
path. The distance is clamped to the valid range [0, length]. Returns two
[Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector) values: the position and the normalized tangent vector.
```lua highlight={10}
function draw(self: PathMeasureDemo, renderer: Renderer)
  -- Draw the base path
  renderer:drawPath(self.path, pathPaint)

  local measure = self.path:measure()
  local len = measure.length

  -- positionAndTangent: place a dot that travels along the path
  local distance = (self.elapsed * 0.3 % 1.0) * len
  local pos, _tan = measure:positionAndTangent(distance)

  self.traveler:reset()
  drawDot(self.traveler, pos.x, pos.y, 8)
  renderer:drawPath(self.traveler, travelerPaint)
end
```


### `warp`

{/* warp: (self: PathMeasure, source: Vector) -> Vector */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
warp(source: Vector) -> Vector
```
</div>

Warps a point onto the path. The x-coordinate of the source point is
interpreted as a distance along the path, and the y-coordinate is used as
an offset along the tangent direction. Returns the warped position as a
[Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector).
```lua highlight={17}
function draw(self: PathMeasureDemo, renderer: Renderer)
  -- Draw the base path
  renderer:drawPath(self.path, pathPaint)

  local measure = self.path:measure()
  local len = measure.length

  -- warp: map a grid of points onto the path using distance (x) and
  -- perpendicular offset (y), then draw a dot at each warped position
  self.warpPath:reset()
  local cols, rows = 16, 3
  local gap = 20
  for col = 0, cols do
    for row = -rows, rows do
      local srcX = (col / cols) * len
      local srcY = row * gap
      local warped = measure:warp(Vector.xy(srcX, srcY))
      drawDot(self.warpPath, warped.x, warped.y, 3)
    end
  end
  renderer:drawPath(self.warpPath, warpPaint)
end
```


### `extract`

{/* extract: (
		self: PathMeasure,
		startDistance: number,
		endDistance: number,
		destination: Path,
		startWithMove: boolean?
	) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
extract(startDistance: number, endDistance: number, destination: Path, startWithMove: boolean?) -> ()
```
</div>

Extracts a sub-section of the path from startDistance to endDistance and
appends it to the destination path. Distances are clamped to the valid
range [0, length]. If startWithMove is true (the default), the extracted
segment begins with a moveTo operation. If false, it continues from the
previous point in the destination path.
```lua highlight={14,17,18}
function draw(self: PathMeasureDemo, renderer: Renderer)
  -- Draw the base path
  renderer:drawPath(self.path, pathPaint)

  local measure = self.path:measure()
  local len = measure.length

  -- extract: animate a highlight window traveling along the path
  local windowSize = len * 0.4
  local startD = (self.elapsed * 0.3 % 1.0) * len
  local endD = startD + windowSize
  self.extractedPath:reset()
  if endD <= len then
    measure:extract(startD, endD, self.extractedPath)
  else
    -- wrap around the end of the path
    measure:extract(startD, len, self.extractedPath)
    measure:extract(0, endD - len, self.extractedPath, false)
  end
  renderer:drawPath(self.extractedPath, extractPaint)
end
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/path/path-data.mdx
==================================================
---
title: PathData
---

PathData is an indexed collection of [PathCommand](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-command) objects.
Both Path and PathData behave like arrays of commands and support iteration via ipairs.


## Methods

### `__len`

{/* function __len(self): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
__len() -> number
```
</div>

Each entry is a [PathCommand](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-command) describing one segment or action in the path.
```lua
for i, command in ipairs(pathData) do
  print(i, command.type)
end
```
Returns the number of commands in the path.
```lua
local count = #pathData
print(count)
```


### `contours`

{/* contours: (self: PathData) -> ContourMeasure? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
contours() -> ContourMeasure?
```
</div>

Returns a [ContourMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/contour-measure) for the first contour in the path. A contour is a
sequence of path segments starting at a `moveTo` and ending before the next
`moveTo` (or end of path). Use the `next` property on the returned
[ContourMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/contour-measure) to iterate through subsequent contours. Returns `nil` if the
path has no contours.
```lua
local contour = pathData:contours()
while contour do
  print(contour.length)
  contour = contour.next
end
```


### `measure`

{/* measure: (self: PathData) -> PathMeasure */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
measure() -> PathMeasure
```
</div>

Returns a [PathMeasure](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-measure) that measures the entire path across all contours.
This provides the total length and allows operations on the path as a whole.
```lua
local measure = pathData:measure()
print(measure.length)
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/path/command-type.mdx
==================================================
---
title: CommandType
---

Describes the type of drawing command stored in a [PathCommand](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-command).

For more information on the following command types, see [Path](/scripting/api-reference/path/path).

- `none` – Placeholder command with no effect. You should not normally see this.
- `moveTo`
- `lineTo`
- `cubicTo`
- `quadTo`
- `close`
```lua highlight={5}
local path = Path.new()
path:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
path:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 0))

for i, command in ipairs(path) do
  print(i, command.type)
end
-- 1 moveTo
-- 2 lineTo
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/image/image-wrap.mdx
==================================================
---
title: ImageWrap
---

Defines how texture coordinates outside the [0, 1] range are handled.
* `clamp`
* `repeat`
* `mirror`

See [ImageSampler](/scripting/api-reference/image/image-sampler) for usage.
```lua highlight={5,7}
function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
  self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
  self.sampler = ImageSampler(
    -- Image wrap X
    'clamp',
    -- Image wrap Y
    'clamp',
    'bilinear'
  )

  return true
end
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/image/image-filter.mdx
==================================================
---
title: ImageFilter
---

Defines how image sampling is performed when scaling or transforming the
image.
* `bilinear`
* `nearest`

See [ImageSampler](/scripting/api-reference/image/image-sampler) for usage.
```lua highlight={6}
function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
  self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
  self.sampler = ImageSampler(
    'clamp',
    'clamp',
    'bilinear'
  )

  return true
end
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/image/image-sampler.mdx
==================================================
---
title: ImageSampler
---

Represents sampling parameters applied when drawing an image, including
wrapping and filtering behaviour.
See also [ImageSampler](/scripting/api-reference/image/image-sampler), [ImageWrap](/scripting/api-reference/image/image-wrap), and [ImageFilter](/scripting/api-reference/image/image-filter).

Check out [Scripting demos](/scripting/demos) to see a working example.

```lua highlight={3,8,15}
type DrawImage = {
  myImage: Image?,
  sampler: ImageSampler?,
}

function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
  self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
  self.sampler = ImageSampler('clamp', 'clamp', 'bilinear')

  return true
end

function draw(self: DrawImage, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler then
    renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
  end
end

return function(): Node<DrawImage>
  return {
    myImage = nil,
    sampler = nil,
    init = init,
    draw = draw,
  }
end
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/image/image.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Image
---

Represents an image asset that can be drawn by the [Renderer](/scripting/api-reference/renderer/renderer).
```lua highlight={2,7,15}
type DrawImage = {
  myImage: Image?,
  sampler: ImageSampler?,
}

function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
  self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
  self.sampler = ImageSampler('clamp', 'clamp', 'bilinear')

  return true
end

function draw(self: DrawImage, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.myImage and self.sampler then
    renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
  end
end

return function(): Node<DrawImage>
  return {
    myImage = nil,
    sampler = nil,
    init = init,
    draw = draw,
  }
end
```


## Fields

### `width`

Width of the image, or `0` until it has decoded. Web runtimes and the
CLI preview decode images after `init` runs, so read it when you use
it, not once in `init`.
```lua highlight={4}
self.myImage = context:image('myImage')

if self.myImage then
    print("myImage width:", self.myImage.width)
end
```


### `height`

Height of the image, or `0` until it has decoded. Web runtimes and the
CLI preview decode images after `init` runs, so read it when you use
it, not once in `init`.
```lua highlight={4}
self.myImage = context:image('myImage')

if self.myImage then
    print("myImage height:", self.myImage.height)
end
```


## Methods

### `view`

{/* function view(self): GPUTextureView */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
view() -> GPUTextureView
```
</div>

Returns a GPUTextureView for sampling this image in WGSL shaders.
The view wraps the underlying GPU texture directly — no copy or decode.
Requires a GPU context (only available when the file uses GPU canvases).
An `ImageAsset`'s view samples its pixels once the image has decoded;
on the web that is after `init`, so take the view once `width` is
above 0.

---
title: Tests
---

A function that defines a collection of test cases. The [Tester](/scripting/api-reference/testing/tester) is provided
to allow cases and groups to be declared.

See [Unit Testing](/scripting/debugging/unit-testing) for usage.




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/testing/expectation.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Expectation
---

Represents an expectation used within a test case. Each method performs an
assertion comparing the supplied value to the expected one.


## Fields

### `never`

Returns an [Expectation](/scripting/api-reference/testing/expectation) that negates the subsequent assertion.
```lua
expect(5).never.is(3)
expect(5).never.greaterThan(10)
```


## Methods

### `is`

{/* is: (any) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
is(any) -> ()
```
</div>

Asserts that the value equals the expected value.
```lua
expect(5).is(5)
expect("hello").is("hello")
```


### `greaterThan`

{/* greaterThan: (any) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
greaterThan(any) -> ()
```
</div>

Asserts that the value is greater than the expected value.
```lua
expect(10).greaterThan(5)
```


### `lessThan`

{/* lessThan: (any) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lessThan(any) -> ()
```
</div>

Asserts that the value is less than the expected value.
```lua
expect(3).lessThan(10)
```


### `greaterThanOrEqual`

{/* greaterThanOrEqual: (any) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
greaterThanOrEqual(any) -> ()
```
</div>

Asserts that the value is greater than or equal to the expected value.
```lua
expect(5).greaterThanOrEqual(5)
expect(6).greaterThanOrEqual(5)
```


### `lessThanOrEqual`

{/* lessThanOrEqual: (any) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lessThanOrEqual(any) -> ()
```
</div>

Asserts that the value is less than or equal to the expected value.
```lua
expect(5).lessThanOrEqual(5)
expect(4).lessThanOrEqual(5)
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/testing/tester.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Tester
---

Provides functions for defining test cases and organizing them into groups.


## Methods

### `case`

{/* case: (name: string, test: (expect: (value: any) -> Expectation) -> ()) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
case(name: string, test: (expect:(value: any) -> Expectation) ->()) -> ()
```
</div>

Defines a named test case. The callback receives an `expect` function
used to create expectations on a value.
```lua
case("adds two numbers", function(expect)
  local result = 2 + 3
  expect(result).is(5)
end)
```


### `errors`

{/* errors: (name: string, test: (expect: (value: any) -> Expectation) -> (), message: string?) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
errors(name: string, test: (expect:(value: any) -> Expectation) ->(), message: string?) -> ()
```
</div>

Defines a test case that passes only when the callback raises an
error. With a `message`, the error must also contain it.
```lua
errors("rejects a negative size", function(expect)
  buffer.create(-1)
end, "invalid argument")
```


### `group`

{/* group: (name: string, test: () -> ()) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
group(name: string, test: () ->()) -> ()
```
</div>

Groups related test cases under a common name. Nested groups are supported.
```lua
group("Math utilities", function()
  case("adds numbers", function(expect)
    expect(2 + 2).is(4)
  end)

  case("multiplies numbers", function(expect)
    expect(3 * 4).is(12)
  end)
end)
```


### `blob`

{/* blob: (name: string) -> Blob? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
blob(name: string) -> Blob?
```
</div>

Looks up a blob asset in the file by name, or nil when missing.
```lua
local data = test.blob("fixtures")
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/text/text.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Text
---

Shapes and lays out styled runs of text with the runtime's shaper, so
scripts get real line breaking and bidirectional ordering. Append runs,
set the box, then draw it in one call or walk its lines and glyphs to draw
them yourself. Codepoint indices are 1 based like `utf8.offset`.
```lua highlight={8,9,10,11,15}
type Label = {
  text: Text,
  paint: Paint,
}

function init(self: Label, context: Context): boolean
  local font = context:font('IBM Plex Sans Arabic')
  self.text:append('مرحبا بالعالم', { font = font, size = 32, paint = self.paint })
  self.text.sizing = 'fixed'
  self.text.maxWidth = 240
  self.text.align = 'start'
  return true
end

function draw(self: Label, renderer: Renderer)
  self.text:draw(renderer)
end
```


## Fields

### `sizing`

### `overflow`

### `align`

### `wrap`

### `wordBreak`

### `origin`

### `direction`

### `maxWidth`

Wrap width when sizing is not 'autoWidth'.


### `maxHeight`

Height the text overflows at when sizing is 'fixed'.


### `paragraphSpacing`

Space between paragraphs separated by a newline.


### `length`

Number of codepoints appended.


### `isEmpty`

### `lineCount`

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/text/font.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Font
---

A font that shapes and draws text. Fonts come from the file's assets with
`context:font(name)`, from a view model `Property<Font>`, or from bytes with
`Font.decode`. Metrics are for a 1 point font and grow negative upwards,
so multiply by the size and expect `ascent` below zero.
```lua highlight={6}
type Label = {
  text: Text,
}

function init(self: Label, context: Context): boolean
  local font = context:font('Inter')
  if font then
    self.text:append('Hello', { font = font, size = 24, paint = Paint.new() })
  end
  return true
end
```


## Fields

### `ascent`

Distance from the baseline to the top of the em box for a 1 point font, negative.


### `descent`

Distance from the baseline to the bottom of the em box for a 1 point font.


### `capHeight`

Distance from the baseline to the top of capital letters, negative.


### `xHeight`

Distance from the baseline to the top of lowercase letters, negative.


### `weight`

Weight from 1 to 1000, 400 being regular.


### `isItalic`

### `axes`

Variable axes the font offers.


### `features`

Four letter OpenType feature tags the font offers, such as 'liga'.


## Static Functions

### `decode`

{/* decode: (bytes: buffer) -> Font? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
decode(bytes: buffer) -> Font?
```
</div>

Decodes a TrueType or OpenType font from bytes a script obtained
itself, such as a downloaded file. Font files in a project are font
assets, reached with `context:font`, not blobs. Returns nil when the
bytes are not a font.
```lua
local font = Font.decode(downloadedBytes)
```


## Methods

### `lineHeight`

{/* function lineHeight(self, size: number): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
lineHeight(size: number) -> number
```
</div>

Height of one line of text at the given size.


### `hasGlyph`

{/* function hasGlyph(self, codepoint: number): boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
hasGlyph(codepoint: number) -> boolean
```
</div>

Whether the font has a glyph for the unicode codepoint.


### `axisValue`

{/* function axisValue(self, tag: string): number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
axisValue(tag: string) -> number
```
</div>

Current value of a variable axis, by tag.


### `withOptions`

{/* function withOptions(self, axes: { [string]: number }?, features: { [string]: number }?): Font */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
withOptions(axes: {[string]: number}?, features: {[string]: number}?) -> Font
```
</div>

A new font at the given axis values and feature settings.
```lua
local bold = font:withOptions({ wght = 700 }, { liga = 0 })
```


### `glyphPath`

{/* function glyphPath(self, glyphId: number): Path */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
glyphPath(glyphId: number) -> Path
```
</div>

Outline of one glyph in 1 point units with the baseline at y 0, wound
for a clockwise fill. Scale by the font size to draw it.

---
title: TextLine
---

One line of a [Text](/scripting/api-reference/text/text) after wrapping. Iterate it to visit its glyphs in
visual order, left to right, whatever the writing direction.
```lua
for _, line in text:lines() do
  for _, glyph in line do
    renderer:save()
    renderer:transform(glyph.transform)
    renderer:drawPath(glyph.font:glyphPath(glyph.id), paint)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end
```


## Fields

### `index`

1 based index of the line within the text.


### `x`

Left edge after alignment.


### `top`

### `bottom`

### `width`

### `direction`

Base direction of the paragraph the line belongs to.


### `firstIndex`

First and last codepoint index on the line, 1 based.


### `lastIndex`

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/artboards/animation.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Animation
---

## Fields

### `duration`

The duration of the animation.
```lua highlight={3}
function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
  if self.anim
    print(self.anim.duration)
  end
  return true
end
```


## Methods

### `advance`

{/* advance: (self: Animation, seconds: number) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
advance(seconds: number) -> boolean
```
</div>

Advances the animation by the given time in seconds. Returns true if the
animation hasn't reached its end. If the animation is set to loop or ping
pong, it will always return true
```lua highlight={23}
type AnimationExample = {
  -- Artboard input, assigned in the Rive editor by the designer
  character: Input<Artboard<nil>>,

  -- The live instance and its animation
  artboardInstance: Artboard<nil>?,
  anim: Animation?,
}

function init(self: AnimationExample, context: Context): boolean
  self.artboardInstance = self.character:instance()

  if self.artboardInstance then
    self.anim = self.artboardInstance:animation('Idle')
  end

  return true
end

function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
  if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    -- Advance the animation to apply keyframe values to the artboard
    self.anim:advance(seconds * 2)
    -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
  end
  return true
end

function draw(self: AnimationExample, renderer: Renderer)
  if self.artboardInstance then
    renderer:save()
    self.artboardInstance:draw(renderer)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end

return function(): Node<AnimationExample>
  return {
    character = late(),
    artboardInstance = nil,
    anim = nil,
    init = init,
    advance = advance,
    draw = draw,
  }
end
```


### `setTime`

{/* setTime: (self: Animation, time: number) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
setTime(time: number) -> ()
```
</div>

set the animation time in seconds
```lua highlight={4}
function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
  if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    -- Set the animation to a specific time in seconds
    self.anim:setTime(0.3)
    -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
  end
  return true
end
```


### `setTimeFrames`

{/* setTimeFrames: (self: Animation, frames: number) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
setTimeFrames(frames: number) -> ()
```
</div>

set the animation time in frames
```lua highlight={4}
function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
  if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    -- Set the animation to a specific frame
    self.anim:setTimeFrames(3)
    -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
  end
  return true
end
```


### `setTimePercentage`

{/* setTimePercentage: (self: Animation, percentage: number) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
setTimePercentage(percentage: number) -> ()
```
</div>

set the animation time as a percentage of the duration
```lua highlight={4}
function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
  if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    -- Set the animation to a specific percentage of the duration.
    self.anim:setTimePercentage(.5)
    -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
  end
  return true
end
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/artboards/scroll-event.mdx
==================================================
---
title: ScrollEvent
---

A scroll from a mouse wheel or a trackpad, delivered to `pointerScroll`.
Direct touch arrives as pointer events instead.
```lua
function pointerScroll(self: ZoomView, event: ScrollEvent)
  self.zoom *= math.exp(-event.delta.y * 0.01)
  event:hit()
end
```


## Fields

### `id`

The unique identifier for the pointer.


### `position`

The pointer's position in local coordinates.


### `delta`

How far the content should travel, in local coordinates. It follows
the content, as a `ScrollConstraint` does, so revealing content
further down reads as a negative `y`.


### `phase`

Where the event sits within its gesture.


### `precise`

True for a pixel precise source like a trackpad, false for a mouse
wheel that moves in detents.


### `timeStamp`

When the scroll happened, in seconds.


## Constructors

### `new`

{/* new: (
        id: number,
        position: Vector,
        delta: Vector,
        phase: ScrollPhase?,
        precise: boolean?,
        timeStamp: number?
    ) -> ScrollEvent */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
new(id: number, position: Vector, delta: Vector, phase: ScrollPhase?, precise: boolean?, timeStamp: number?) -> ScrollEvent
```
</div>

Creates a new [ScrollEvent](/scripting/api-reference/artboards/scroll-event). The phase defaults to `update` and precise
to false, as a mouse wheel reports them.
```lua highlight={1}
local wheel = ScrollEvent.new(0, Vector.xy(10, 20), Vector.xy(0, -40))
print(wheel.phase, wheel.precise)
```


## Methods

### `hit`

{/* hit: (self: ScrollEvent) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
hit() -> ()
```
</div>

Claims the scroll. Without it the scroll passes to whatever lies
behind, such as a `ScrollConstraint` view. A claimed trackpad gesture
stays with this node until it ends.

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/artboards/pointer-event.mdx
==================================================
---
title: PointerEvent
---

Represents a pointer interaction event containing position and pointer id.


## Fields

### `position`

The position of the pointer in local coordinates.
```lua highlight={10,11}
function handlePointerDown(self: RenderInstance, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local localPos = event.position - Vector.xy(self.x, self.y)
    local localEvent = PointerEvent.new(event.id, localPos)
    local hit = self.instance:pointerDown(localEvent)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(
        string.format(
          'Local hit at (%.1f, %.1f)',
          localEvent.position.x,
          localEvent.position.y
        )
      )
    end
  end
end
```


### `id`

The unique identifier for the pointer.
```lua highlight={7}
function handlePointerDown(self: RenderInstance, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local localPos = event.position - Vector.xy(self.x, self.y)
    local localEvent = PointerEvent.new(event.id, localPos)
    local hit = self.instance:pointerDown(localEvent)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(localEvent.id)
    end
  end
end
```


### `type`

The type of event (pointerDown, pointerUp, click, pointerEnter, pointerMove, etc).


### `previousPosition`

The pointer's previous position in local coordinates. Node pointer
handlers read the origin.


### `timeStamp`

When the interaction happened, in seconds.


## Constructors

### `new`

{/* new: (id: number, position: Vector) -> PointerEvent */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
new(id: number, position: Vector) -> PointerEvent
```
</div>

Creates a new [PointerEvent](/scripting/api-reference/artboards/pointer-event) with the given id and position.
```lua highlight={4}
function handlePointerDown(self: RenderInstance, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local localPos = event.position - Vector.xy(self.x, self.y)
    local localEvent = PointerEvent.new(event.id, localPos)
    local hit = self.instance:pointerDown(localEvent)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(
        string.format(
          'Local hit at (%.1f, %.1f)',
          localEvent.position.x,
          localEvent.position.y
        )
      )
    end
  end
end
```


## Methods

### `hit`

{/* hit: (self: PointerEvent, isTranslucent:boolean?) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
hit(isTranslucent: boolean?) -> ()
```
</div>

Consumes the event. Call it on every event a script owns -- the press,
each move of a drag, and the release -- or the event keeps travelling
outward and an enclosing hit target claims the gesture. A
`ScrollConstraint` viewport is the usual one: without this, dragging a
control inside a scroll view scrolls the view instead.

The argument inverts. Bare `hit()` is opaque and stops there;
`hit(true)` marks this target translucent, so the event continues to
whatever is behind it.
```lua highlight={6}
function handlePointerDown(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local hit = self.instance:pointerDown(event)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      -- Mark as handled but still allow translucent targets behind to receive it.
      event:hit(true)
    end
  end
end
```

```lua
local event = context:asReportedEvent()
if event then
  print(event.delaySeconds)
end
```

---
title: NodeReadData
---

Represents a node in the hierarchy, providing transform properties and
access to parent and child nodes.


## Fields

### `position`

The local position of the node.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.position = Vector.xy(199, 299)
  end
end
```


### `rotation`

The local rotation of the node in radians.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.rotation = math.rad(45)
  end
end
```


### `scale`

The local scale of the node.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.scale = Vector.xy(1.4, 2)
  end
end
```


### `worldTransform`

The read-only world transform of the node.
```lua highlight={4,5,6,7}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    local wt = node.worldTransform
    print("world xx:", wt.xx, "xy:", wt.xy)
    print("world yx:", wt.yx, "yy:", wt.yy)
    print("world tx:", wt.tx, "ty:", wt.ty)
  end
end
```


### `x`

The x-coordinate of the local position.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.x = 100
  end
end
```


### `y`

The y-coordinate of the local position.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.y = 200
  end
end
```


### `scaleX`

The x component of the local scale.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.scaleX = 2
  end
end
```


### `scaleY`

The y component of the local scale.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    node.scaleY = 2
  end
end
```


### `paint`

The stroke or fill a path effect applies to, on the node its `update`
receives, otherwise nil. The same as `asPaint`.
```lua highlight={2}
function update(self: MyEffect, path: PathData, node: NodeReadData): PathData
  local paint = node.paint
  if paint then
    print(paint.color)
  end
  return path
end
```


## Methods

### `asPath`

{/* function asPath(self):  PathData? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
asPath() -> PathData?
```
</div>

If node is a Path, returns the node as [PathData](/scripting/api-reference/path/path-data).
```lua highlight={5}
function pointerDown(self: PaintInstance, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local myPath = self.instance:node('MyPath')
    if myPath then
      local path = myPath:asPath()
      if path then
        local cmd: PathCommand = path[1]
        print(cmd.type) -- moveTo
      end
    end
  end
end
```


### `asPaint`

{/* function asPaint(self):  Paint? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
asPaint() -> Paint?
```
</div>

Returns the stroke or fill a path effect applies to, on the node its
`update` receives, otherwise nil.
```lua highlight={2}
function update(self: MyEffect, path: PathData, node: NodeReadData): PathData
  local paint = node:asPaint()
  if paint then
    print(paint.thickness)
  end
  return path
end
```

---
title: Artboard
---

Represents a Rive artboard instance, providing drawing, advancing,
interaction handling, and access to [named nodes](/editor/exporting/exporting-names) and data.


## Fields

### `frameOrigin`

If true, the artboard’s origin is treated as the frame origin.
```lua highlight={6}
function init(self: RenderInstance, context: Context): boolean
  local vm = Data.Character.new()

  self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
  if self.instance then
    self.instance.frameOrigin = true
  end

  return true
end
```


### `data`

The typed data associated with the artboard.
```lua highlight={9,10,11,12}
function init(self: RenderInstance, context: Context): boolean
  local vm = Data.Character.new()

  self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)

  if self.instance then
    self.instance.frameOrigin = true

    local data = self.instance.data
    if data then
      print(data.nickname)
    end
  end

  return true
end
```


### `width`

The width of the artboard.
```lua
self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
  if self.instance then
    print(self.instance.width)
  end
end
```


### `height`

The height of the artboard.
```lua
self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
  if self.instance then
    print(self.instance.height)
  end
end
```


## Methods

### `draw`

{/* draw: (self: Artboard<T>, renderer: Renderer, visitor: ((context: any, drawable: Drawable, renderer: Renderer) -> ())?, context: any?) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
draw(renderer: Renderer, visitor: ((context: any, drawable: Drawable, renderer: Renderer) ->())?, context: any?) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws the artboard using the provided renderer.
```lua highlight={20}
type RenderInstances = {
  character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,

  instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
}

function init(self: RenderInstances, context: Context): boolean
  local vm = Data.Character.new()

  self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)

  return true
end

function draw(self: RenderInstances, renderer: Renderer)
  local instance = self.instance

  if instance then
    renderer:save()
    instance:draw(renderer)
    renderer:restore()
  end
end

return function(): Node<RenderInstances>
  return {
    character = late(),
    instance = nil,
    init = init,
    draw = draw,
  }
end
```

With a `visitor`, each drawable that has custom properties is handed
to it instead of being drawn: the visitor decides whether to call
`drawable:draw(renderer)` and under what renderer state. Whatever it
sets on the renderer ends with that visit. Every other drawable draws
as usual, and clipping still applies. `context` is passed through to
the visitor untouched.
```lua
-- In init: local GLOW = artboard:propertyKey("glow")
-- Draw only the drawables tagged `glow`, in their own paint.
artboard:draw(renderer, function(context, drawable, renderer)
  if drawable:boolean(GLOW) then
    drawable:draw(renderer)
  end
end)
```

Drawing a tagged nested artboard visits the tagged drawables inside
it from within that `drawable:draw` call, so a value carries down in
a local:
```lua
local level = 1
artboard:draw(renderer, function(context, drawable, renderer)
  local outer = level
  level = outer * math.min(drawable:number(EMISSIVE) or 0, 1)
  local c = math.floor(level * 255)
  renderer:setColorModulation(Color.rgba(c, c, c, 255))
  drawable:draw(renderer)
  level = outer
end)
```


### `drawModulated`

{/* drawModulated: (self: Artboard<T>, renderer: Renderer, key: PropertyKey) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
drawModulated(renderer: Renderer, key: PropertyKey) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws the artboard with the color modulation set, per drawable, from
its custom property of this key: a number as a gray level clamped to
0..1, a color as is. Drawables without it draw under the renderer's
current state. Levels multiply down through tagged drawables that
hold others: inside a nested artboard tagged 0.5, a shape tagged 0.2
draws at 0.1 and an untagged one at 0.5. Nothing calls back into the
script, so this is the cheapest way to draw a pass like emission.
```lua
-- In init: local EMISSIVE = artboard:propertyKey("emissive")
-- Everything black except drawables tagged `emissive`.
renderer:save()
renderer:setColorModulation(Color.rgba(0, 0, 0, 255))
artboard:drawModulated(renderer, EMISSIVE)
renderer:restore()
```


### `propertyKey`

{/* propertyKey: (self: Artboard<T>, name: string) -> PropertyKey */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
propertyKey(name: string) -> PropertyKey
```
</div>

The key custom properties called `name` are read by. When no
property in the file carries that name the key matches nothing, so
every read by it comes back nil. Custom properties are added to a
drawable in the editor's inspector.


### `advance`

{/* advance: (self: Artboard<T>, seconds: number) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
advance(seconds: number) -> boolean
```
</div>

Advances the artboard by the given time in seconds. Returns true if the
artboard should continue receiving advance calls.
```lua highlight={17}
type RenderInstances = {
  character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,

  instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
}

function init(self: RenderInstances, context: Context): boolean
  local vm = Data.Character.new()

  self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)

  return true
end

function advance(self: RenderInstances, seconds: number): boolean
  if self.instance then
    return self.instance:advance(seconds)
  end
  return true
end

return function(): Node<RenderInstances>
  return {
    character = late(),
    instance = nil,
    init = init,
    advance = advance,
  }
end
```


### `instance`

{/* instance: (self: Artboard<T>, viewModel: ViewModel?) -> Artboard<T> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
instance(viewModel: ViewModel?) -> Artboard<T>
```
</div>

Creates a new instance of the artboard with independent state.
```lua highlight={8}
type ViewModelExample = {
  character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,
  instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
}

function init(self: ViewModelExample, context: Context): boolean
  local vm = Data.Character.new()
  self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
  return true
end

return function(): Node<ViewModelExample>
  return {
    character = late(),
    instance = nil,
    init = init,
  }
end
```


### `animation`

{/* animation: (self: Artboard<T>, name: string) -> Animation? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
animation(name: string) -> Animation?
```
</div>

Creates an animation instance linked to the artboard instance


### `bounds`

{/* bounds: (self:Artboard<T>) -> (Vector, Vector) */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
bounds() -> (Vector, Vector)
```
</div>

Returns the bounding box of the artboard as two [Vector](/scripting/api-reference/vector/vector) values: the
minimum point and the maximum point.
```lua
local minPt, maxPt = self.instance:bounds()
print("Bounds width", maxPt.x - minPt.x)
print("Bounds height", maxPt.y - minPt.y)
```


### `node`

{/* node: (self:Artboard<T>, name:string) -> NodeData? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
node(name: string) -> NodeData?
```
</div>

Returns the node with the given name, or nil if no such node exists.
```lua highlight={2}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Root')
  if node then
    local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    node:decompose(m)
  end
end
```


### `pointerDown`

{/* pointerDown: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerDown(event: PointerEvent) -> number
```
</div>

Pointer event down handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
artboard is hit.
```lua highlight={3}
function handlePointerDown(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local hit = self.instance:pointerDown(event)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(event.id)
      print(event.position)
    end
  end
end
```


### `pointerUp`

{/* pointerUp: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerUp(event: PointerEvent) -> number
```
</div>

Pointer event up handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
artboard is hit.
```lua highlight={3}
function handlePointerUp(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local hit = self.instance:pointerUp(event)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(event.id)
      print(event.position)
    end
  end
end
```


### `pointerMove`

{/* pointerMove: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerMove(event: PointerEvent) -> number
```
</div>

Pointer event move handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
artboard is hit.
```lua highlight={3}
function handlePointerMove(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local hit = self.instance:pointerMove(event)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(event.id)
      print(event.position)
    end
  end
end
```


### `pointerExit`

{/* pointerExit: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerExit(event: PointerEvent) -> number
```
</div>

Pointer event exit handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
artboard is hit.
```lua highlight={3}
function handlePointerExit(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local hit = self.instance:pointerExit(event)
    if hit ~= 0 then
      print(event.id)
      print(event.position)
    end
  end
end
```


### `pointerScroll`

{/* pointerScroll: (self: Artboard<T>, event: ScrollEvent) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerScroll(event: ScrollEvent) -> number
```
</div>

Scroll handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit), non-zero when
a `ScrollConstraint` view inside the artboard took the scroll. Claim
the outer event when it does, so the gesture stays with this node.
```lua highlight={12}
function handlePointerScroll(self: RenderInstance, event: ScrollEvent)
  if self.instance then
    local localPos = event.position - Vector.xy(self.x, self.y)
    local localEvent = ScrollEvent.new(
      event.id,
      localPos,
      event.delta,
      event.phase,
      event.precise,
      event.timeStamp
    )
    if self.instance:pointerScroll(localEvent) ~= 0 then
      event:hit()
    end
  end
end
```


### `addToPath`

{/* addToPath: (self:Artboard<T>, path:Path, transform:Mat2D?) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
addToPath(path: Path, transform: Mat2D?) -> ()
```
</div>

Adds the artboard’s geometry to the given path, optionally transformed
by the provided matrix.

For a complete working example, see the [Add to Path](https://rive.app/community/files/27188-51290-add-to-path-scripting-demo?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=scripting_api&utm_campaign=docs_to_marketplace_links) demo.
```lua highlight={18}
function draw(self: AddToPathExample, renderer: Renderer)
  local instance = self.instance
  if not instance then
    return
  end

  -- Draw the artboard normally first.
  renderer:save()
  instance:draw(renderer)
  renderer:restore()

  -- Reset the path each frame, then rebuild it from the artboard's geometry.
  self.outlinePath:reset()

  -- Add the artboard's geometry into the path with an optional transform.
  -- Here we apply a slight offset via Mat2D to show the transform parameter.
  local transform = Mat2D.withTranslation(8, 8)
  instance:addToPath(self.outlinePath, transform)

  -- Draw the extracted path with a custom stroke paint as an outline / shadow effect.
  renderer:drawPath(self.outlinePath, self.outlinePaint)
end
```


### `gamepadConnected`

{/* gamepadConnected: (self: Artboard<T>, event: GamepadConnected) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
gamepadConnected(event: GamepadConnected) -> number
```
</div>

Forwards a gamepad connection to the artboard: its focused control
first, then every scripted node that did not take it. Returns how
many scripted nodes received it.
```lua
function gamepadConnected(self: Forwarder, event: GamepadConnected)
  self.instance:gamepadConnected(event)
end
```


### `gamepadEvent`

{/* gamepadEvent: (self: Artboard<T>, event: GamepadEvent) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
gamepadEvent(event: GamepadEvent) -> number
```
</div>

Forwards a gamepad button or axis change to the artboard, the same way
as `gamepadConnected`.


### `gamepadDisconnected`

{/* gamepadDisconnected: (self: Artboard<T>, event: GamepadDisconnected) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
gamepadDisconnected(event: GamepadDisconnected) -> number
```
</div>

Forwards a gamepad disconnection to the artboard, the same way as
`gamepadConnected`.

---
title: GamepadConnected
---

Full gamepad state when a device is first seen (`gamepadConnected`).
Aligned with W3C Standard Gamepad when `mapping` is `'standard'`.


## Fields

### `deviceId`

Embedder-stable device id for this logical gamepad session.


### `buttonMask`

Bit *i* set when W3C standard button index *i* is pressed.


### `buttons`

Analog value per button (0–1), same order as W3C `buttons[]` / `buttonValues` (1-based).


### `axes`

Analog axes (1-based). Standard layout uses at least six entries (sticks and triggers).


### `isStandardMapping`

Whether the embedder normalized to the standard layout.


### `mapping`

`'standard'` or `'unknown'` (semantic names match only when standard).


### `gamepadMapping`

Raw enum value: 0 = standard, 1 = unknown (same as [GamepadMappingKind](/scripting/api-reference/artboards/gamepad-mapping-kind) order).


### `west`

Face buttons (standard mapping only; otherwise false).


### `south`

### `north`

### `east`

### `leftShoulder`

### `rightShoulder`

### `back`

Select / Start (W3C back / forward).


### `forward`

### `leftStickButton`

Stick click buttons.


### `rightStickButton`

### `dpadUp`

### `dpadDown`

### `dpadLeft`

### `dpadRight`

### `start`

### `leftStick`

Left and right analog stick deflection (axes 0–3 when standard).


### `rightStick`

### `leftTrigger`

Analog shoulder triggers (axes 4–5 when standard).


### `rightTrigger`

### `leftTriggerPressed`

Digital trigger buttons (indices 6–7 when standard).


### `rightTriggerPressed`

## Methods

### `buttonPressed`

{/* buttonPressed: (self: GamepadConnected, index: number) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">

```lua
buttonPressed(index: number) -> boolean
```
</div>

True if W3C button index `index` is pressed (1-based, matches `buttons` / bitmask).


### `buttonValue`

{/* buttonValue: (self: GamepadConnected, index: number) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua

```
</div>

`GamepadButton.value` for the given 1-based button index.


### `axis`

{/* axis: (self: GamepadConnected, index: number) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
axis(index: number) -> number
```
</div>

Axis value for the given 1-based axis index.

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/artboards/node-data.mdx
==================================================
---
title: NodeData
---

Represents a node in the hierarchy, providing transform properties and
access to parent and child nodes.


## Fields

### `children`

The node’s children.
```lua highlight={5}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    local hipsFirstChild = node.children[1]
    print(hipsFirstChild)
    local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)

    if hipsFirstChild then
      hipsFirstChild:decompose(m)
    end
  end
end
```


### `parent`

The parent of the node, or nil if it has none.
```lua highlight={4}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
  if node then
    local hipsParent = node.parent
    local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    if hipsParent then
      hipsParent:decompose(m)
    end
  end
end
```


## Methods

### `decompose`

{/* function decompose(self, worldTransform:Mat2D): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
decompose(worldTransform: Mat2D) -> ()
```
</div>

Updates the node’s position, rotation, and scale from the given world
transform.
```lua highlight={5}
if self.instance then
  local node = self.instance:node('Root')
  if node then
    local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    node:decompose(m)
  end
end
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/artboards/scroll-phase.mdx
==================================================
---
title: ScrollPhase
---

Where a [ScrollEvent](/scripting/api-reference/artboards/scroll-event) sits within its gesture. A mouse wheel only ever
reports `update`.

* `begin`: fingers started a trackpad gesture
* `update`: the gesture moved, or a wheel turned
* `end`: the fingers lifted; hosts whose platform sends its own momentum
never report it
* `momentum`: platform generated travel after the fingers lifted
* `inertiaCancel`: fingers landed during momentum to stop it; carries no
delta

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/artboards/view-model.mdx

---
title: ViewModel
---

Represents a view model used for data binding.

A [ViewModel](/scripting/api-reference/interfaces/view-model) provides structured data that can be read and modified at
runtime, allowing Rive files to react to application state.
```lua
type ViewModelExample = {
  character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,
  instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
}

function init(self: ViewModelExample, context: Context): boolean
  local vm = Data.Character.new()
  self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
  return true
end

return function(): Node<ViewModelExample>
  return {
    character = late(),
    instance = nil,
    init = init,
  }
end
```

---
title: ListenerContext
---

Provides access to the context that triggered a listener action.

A [ListenerContext](/scripting/api-reference/artboards/listener-context) can represent different event types (pointer, keyboard,
text input, focus, view model changes, or reported events). Use the
`is...` methods to check the type, and the corresponding `as...` methods
to retrieve the event data.


## Methods

### `isPointerEvent`

{/* isPointerEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isPointerEvent() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by a pointer event.


### `isKeyboardEvent`

{/* isKeyboardEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isKeyboardEvent() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by a keyboard event.


### `isTextInput`

{/* isTextInput: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isTextInput() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by a text input event.


### `isFocus`

{/* isFocus: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isFocus() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by a focus change.


### `isReportedEvent`

{/* isReportedEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isReportedEvent() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by a reported Rive event.


### `isViewModelChange`

{/* isViewModelChange: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isViewModelChange() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by a view model change.


### `isGamepadConnected`

{/* isGamepadConnected: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isGamepadConnected() -> boolean
```
</div>

### `isGamepadEvent`

{/* isGamepadEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isGamepadEvent() -> boolean
```
</div>

### `isGamepadDisconnected`

{/* isGamepadDisconnected: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isGamepadDisconnected() -> boolean
```
</div>

### `isNone`

{/* isNone: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
isNone() -> boolean
```
</div>

Returns true if the action was triggered by an unknown or unsupported event type.


### `asPointerEvent`

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/file-format/format-view.mdx
==================================================
---
title: FormatView
---

A live preview of one document on one surface. Created by
`FileFormat.view`; disposed when its surface closes.


## Methods

### `draw`

{/* draw: (self: FormatView, renderer: Renderer,
        width: number, height: number) -> () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
draw(renderer: Renderer, width: number, height: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Draws the current frame into a viewport of width by height.


### `measure`

{/* measure: ((self: FormatView, viewportWidth: number,
        viewportHeight: number) -> (number, number))? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
measure(viewportWidth: number, viewportHeight: number) -> (number, number)
```
</div>

Pane surfaces only: the content's intrinsic size for the given
viewport, driving the pane's scrollbars. Called when the view is
created, the document changes, the viewport resizes, or requestDraw
fires. Omit for fit-to-viewport views; the inspector never measures.


### `advance`

{/* advance: ((self: FormatView, seconds: number) -> boolean)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
advance(seconds: number) -> boolean
```
</div>

Advances animation state. Return true to keep receiving frames.


### `textScrolled`

{/* textScrolled: ((self: FormatView, x: number, y: number,
        line: number, maxLine: number) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
textScrolled(x: number, y: number, line: number, maxLine: number) -> ()
```
</div>

The user scrolled the text editor. x/y are scroll percentages and
line is the fractional top visible line. Never fired for scrolls the
host performed on the view's behalf (scrollEditorTo), so handlers can
follow without echo bookkeeping.


### `paneScrolled`

{/* paneScrolled: ((self: FormatView, x: number, y: number) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
paneScrolled(x: number, y: number) -> ()
```
</div>

The user scrolled the preview pane (measured views only). x/y are the
new offsets in content coordinates. Never fired for scrolls the host
applied from `editor:scrollTo`.


### `paneWheel`

{/* paneWheel: ((self: FormatView, dx: number, dy: number) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
paneWheel(dx: number, dy: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Raw wheel/trackpad input over an unmeasured (self-scrolling) preview,
in pixels with positive y scrolling down. Implement to route pane
input into the view's own scrolling; without it the host falls back
to scrolling the paired text editor.


### `pointerDown`

{/* pointerDown: ((self: FormatView, event: PointerEvent) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerDown(event: PointerEvent) -> ()
```
</div>

Pointer input over the preview surface, in the same coordinate space
draw receives. Signatures match the Layout protocol so live artboards
can forward events directly (board:pointerDown(event), ...).


### `pointerMove`

{/* pointerMove: ((self: FormatView, event: PointerEvent) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerMove(event: PointerEvent) -> ()
```
</div>

### `pointerUp`

{/* pointerUp: ((self: FormatView, event: PointerEvent) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
pointerUp(event: PointerEvent) -> ()
```
</div>

### `documentChanged`

{/* documentChanged: ((self: FormatView, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
documentChanged(doc: FormatDocument, parsed: buffer?) -> ()
```
</div>

Text documents only: the document changed; refresh derived state.


### `selectionChanged`

{/* selectionChanged: ((self: FormatView, line: number,
        column: number) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
selectionChanged(line: number, column: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Text documents only: the primary cursor moved. line and column are
zero based code point coordinates.


### `dispose`

{/* dispose: ((self: FormatView) -> ())? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
dispose() -> ()
```
</div>

The surface is closing; release resources.

File extension of the document without the dot, e.g. "md".

---
title: EditorScroll
---

Scroll position of the text editor pane showing this document. `line` is
the fractional 0-based line at the top of the viewport: 10.5 means the
viewport top sits halfway through line 10. `percent` runs 0 to 1 across
the editor's scrollable range.


## Fields

### `percent`

### `line`

### `maxLine`

Scrollable range in line units (the top line when fully scrolled).


### `cursorLine`

The primary cursor's line, and where it sits in the viewport
(0 top to 1 bottom, outside that range when off screen). Nil when
the editor has no cursor.


### `cursorFraction`

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/file-format/editor-context.mdx
==================================================
---
title: EditorContext
---

Edit time context handed to FileFormat views. Everything it returns is
either immutable or a private instance; nothing reaches back into the
open file's live state.


## Methods

### `image`

{/* function image(self, name: string): Image? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
image(name: string) -> Image?
```
</div>

Looks up an image asset by name, or nil when missing.


### `blob`

{/* function blob(self, name: string): Blob? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
blob(name: string) -> Blob?
```
</div>

Looks up a blob asset by name, or nil when missing.


### `artboard`

{/* function artboard(self, name: string): Artboard<ViewModel?>? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
artboard(name: string) -> Artboard<ViewModel?>?
```
</div>

A fresh instance of a named artboard, private to this view. The
artboard's default view model instance is bound and reachable through
`data`, nil when the artboard has no view model.

Names resolve against this script's own file, so a format shipped in a
library reaches that library's artboards. Prefix a name with a
library's namespace (`markdown@0/Document`) to name one explicitly,
and use `hostArtboard` for the file being edited.


### `hostArtboard`

{/* function hostArtboard(self, name: string): Artboard<ViewModel?>? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
hostArtboard(name: string) -> Artboard<ViewModel?>?
```
</div>

Like `artboard`, but always resolves in the file being edited. When
this script is authored in that same file the two are identical, so a
library developed in place behaves as it does once shipped.


### `theme`

{/* function theme(self): EditorTheme */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
theme() -> EditorTheme
```
</div>

The editor's current theme.


### `openUrl`

{/* function openUrl(self, url: string) */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
openUrl(url: string)
```
</div>

Opens a url in the user's browser.


### `themeFont`

{/* function themeFont(self): Font? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
themeFont() -> Font?
```
</div>

The font the code editor renders with, for previews that want to
match its typography. Assign to a view model font property.


### `defaultFont`

{/* function defaultFont(self): Font? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
defaultFont() -> Font?
```
</div>

The editor's default UI font, for preview prose. Assign to a view
model font property.


### `codeFont`

{/* function codeFont(self): Font? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
codeFont() -> Font?
```
</div>

The editor's built-in code font, for preview code regions. Assign to
a view model font property.


### `editorScroll`

{/* function editorScroll(self): EditorScroll? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
editorScroll() -> EditorScroll?
```
</div>

The text editor's scroll position, refreshed each draw while the user
scrolls, or nil on surfaces without an attached editor (inspector,
viewer tab). Use with `scrollTo` to keep the preview in sync.


### `scrollTo`

{/* function scrollTo(self, x: number, y: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
scrollTo(x: number, y: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Scrolls the pane hosting this view to a content offset, clamped to
the measured content. Only meaningful for pane views with `measure`;
elsewhere it is ignored.


### `scrollEditorTo`

{/* function scrollEditorTo(self, line: number): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
scrollEditorTo(line: number) -> ()
```
</div>

Scrolls the attached text editor to a fractional line factor (the
same unit `editorScroll` reports), clamped to the editor's range.
Ignored without an attached editor. Guard against ping-pong when
combining with `editorScroll` driven syncing.


### `requestDraw`

{/* function requestDraw(self): () */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
requestDraw() -> ()
```
</div>

Asks the host to repaint the view outside the advance loop, e.g. when
an async decode completes.


### `shader`

{/* function shader(self, name: string): Shader? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
shader(name: string) -> Shader?
```
</div>

Looks up a compiled shader by name, or nil when missing.


### `canvas`

{/* function canvas(self, desc: { width: number?, height: number? }?): Canvas */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
canvas(desc: {width: number?, height: number?}?) -> Canvas
```
</div>

Creates a CPU canvas. Zero or missing size defers the backing
texture.


### `gpuCanvas`

{/* function gpuCanvas(self, desc: { width: number?, height: number? }?): GPUCanvas */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
gpuCanvas(desc: {width: number?, height: number?}?) -> GPUCanvas
```
</div>

Creates a GPU canvas for render pass drawing. Zero or missing size
defers the backing texture.


### `features`

{/* function features(self): GPUFeatures */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
features() -> GPUFeatures
```
</div>

Capabilities of the active GPU device.


### `decodeImage`

{/* function decodeImage(self, data: buffer): Promise<DecodedImage> */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
decodeImage(data: buffer) -> Promise<DecodedImage>
```
</div>

Decodes an encoded image (png, jpeg, webp) into a drawable image.

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/file-format/file-format.mdx
==================================================
---
title: FileFormat
---

Implement this protocol to add editor support for a custom binary file
format. Files with a claimed extension import as blobs, keeping their raw
bytes, and get previews from `view`. For text formats that should be
editable in the editor, implement TextFileFormat instead.
```lua
local format: FileFormat = {
    name = 'Model',
    extensions = { 'glb' },
}

return function(): FileFormat
    return format
end
```


## Fields

### `name`

Display name of the format, e.g. "Markdown".


### `extensions`

File extensions handled, without dots, e.g. `{"md", "markdown"}`.


## Methods

### `parse`

{/* parse: ((self: FileFormat, doc: FormatDocument) -> buffer?)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
parse(doc: FormatDocument) -> buffer?
```
</div>

Optional. Called once per document version; the returned buffer is
cached by Rive, keyed to the document's content, and passed back into
every other callback. Within one VM the same buffer object is reused;
across VMs the bytes are copied once.


### `view`

{/* view: ((self: FileFormat,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        editor: EditorContext,
        surface: FormatSurface,
        parsed: buffer?) -> FormatView?)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
view(doc: FormatDocument, editor: EditorContext, surface: FormatSurface, parsed: buffer?) -> FormatView?
```
</div>

Creates the preview for a document on a surface. Each surface gets
its own view; a document can be visible on several at once.

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/file-format/text-file-format.mdx
==================================================
---
title: TextFileFormat
---

A FileFormat for text. Files with a claimed extension import as in-band
text documents, editable in the editor and synced across collaborators,
and the callbacks below drive the text editor's intelligence. Documents
export as plain blobs, so scripts read them via `context:blob(name)` at
both edit time and runtime.

Analysis callbacks are pure functions of `(doc, parsed)`; state lives
only in views. `parsed` carries the cached result of `parse`, or nil when
`parse` is not implemented.
```lua
local format: TextFileFormat = {
    name = 'Markdown',
    extensions = { 'md' },
}

return function(): TextFileFormat
    return format
end
```


## Fields

### `name`

Display name of the format, e.g. "Markdown".


### `extensions`

File extensions handled, without dots, e.g. `{"md", "markdown"}`.


## Methods

### `parse`

{/* parse: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument) -> buffer?)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
parse(doc: FormatDocument) -> buffer?
```
</div>

Optional. Called once per document version; the returned buffer is
cached by Rive, keyed to the document's content, and passed back into
every other callback. Within one VM the same buffer object is reused;
across VMs the bytes are copied once.


### `view`

{/* view: ((self: TextFileFormat,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        editor: EditorContext,
        surface: FormatSurface,
        parsed: buffer?) -> FormatView?)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
view(doc: FormatDocument, editor: EditorContext, surface: FormatSurface, parsed: buffer?) -> FormatView?
```
</div>

Creates the preview for a document on a surface. Each surface gets
its own view; a document can be visible on several at once.


### `highlight`

{/* highlight: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatToken})? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
highlight(doc: FormatDocument, parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatToken}
```
</div>

Returns highlight tokens for the document.


### `diagnostics`

{/* diagnostics: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatDiagnostic})? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
diagnostics(doc: FormatDocument, parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatDiagnostic}
```
</div>

Returns problems for the document.


### `completions`

{/* completions: ((self: TextFileFormat,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        line: number,
        column: number,
        parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatCompletion})? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
completions(doc: FormatDocument, line: number, column: number, parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatCompletion}
```
</div>

Returns completions at the given position.


### `hover`

{/* hover: ((self: TextFileFormat,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        line: number,
        column: number,
        parsed: buffer?) -> FormatHover?)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
hover(doc: FormatDocument, line: number, column: number, parsed: buffer?) -> FormatHover?
```
</div>

Returns hover documentation at the given position, or nil.


### `format`

{/* format: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> string?)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
format(doc: FormatDocument, parsed: buffer?) -> string?
```
</div>

Returns the fully formatted text, or nil to leave the document
unchanged. Rive diffs the result against the current text and applies
minimal edits.




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/interfaces/converter.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Converter
---

A scripted converter used for transforming values between ViewModel data
bindings and Rive properties.

Type parameters:
T: The converter type
I: The input type, must be a DataValue type
(DataValueNumber, DataValueString, DataValueBoolean, DataValueColor, etc)
O: The output type, must be a DataValue type
(DataValueNumber, DataValueString, DataValueBoolean, DataValueColor, etc)

For more information, see [Converter Scripts](/scripting/protocols/converter-scripts).


## Methods

### `init`

{/* init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
init(self: T, context: Context) -> boolean
```
</div>

Called once when the converter is created. Returns true if initialization
succeeds.
```lua
-- Called once when the script initializes.
function init(self: MyConverter, context: Context): boolean

    -- Return false to stop the script.
    return true
end
```


### `convert`

{/* convert: (self: T, input: I) -> O */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
convert(self: T, input: I) -> O
```
</div>

Converts the input value (a view model property) to an output value.
The input parameter must be a DataValue type.
```lua
-- Converts the value when binding from source to target.
function convert(self: MyConverter, input: DataInputs): DataOutput

  local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
  if input:isNumber() then
    -- Example: Add 1 to the incoming number
    dv.value = (input :: DataValueNumber).value + 1
  end
  return dv
end
```


### `reverseConvert`

{/* reverseConvert: (self: T, input: O) -> I */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
reverseConvert(self: T, input: O) -> I
```
</div>

Converts the output value back to an input value (a view model property).
The input parameter must be a DataValue type.
```lua
function reverseConvert(
  self: MyConverter,
  input: DataOutput
): DataInputs
  local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
  if input:isNumber() then
    -- Example: Subract 1 from the target number
    dv.value = (input :: DataValueNumber).value - 1
  end
  return dv
end
```


### `advance`

{/* advance: ((self: T, seconds: number) -> boolean)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
advance(self: T, seconds: number) -> boolean
```
</div>

Optional per-frame update. Returns true if the converter should continue
receiving advance calls.
```lua
function advance(self: MyConverter, seconds: number): boolean
  return false
end
```

TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/interfaces/input.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Input
---

Represents a typed input value.
```lua highlight={3,4,5,6}
-- Define the script's data and inputs.
type MyNode = {
  speed: Input<number>,
  title: Input<string>,
  enabled: Input<boolean>,
  onReset: Input<Trigger>,
}

-- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
return function(): Node<MyNode>
  return {
    speed = 1,
    title = 'Rive so coooool!',
    enabled = false,
    onReset = function() end,
  }
end
```




==================================================
TOPIC: rive-docs/scripting/api-reference/interfaces/interpolator.mdx
==================================================
---
title: Interpolator
---

An interpolator: eases keyframes, state transitions, layout animations and
interpolating data converters.

Rive creates an instance per owner instance: each playing animation gets one
per keyframe, each state machine one per interpolator its transitions use,
each artboard one per interpolator its layout styles use, and each bound
converter its own. Transitions or layout styles that use the same
interpolator share its instance, as do layouts that inherit their animation
from a parent layout (including nested artboards and list items).

So `transform` and `transformValue` can be called many times per frame, by
several layouts, in any order. Compute the result from `value` (and `from`
and `to`), the inputs and whatever `init` set up; don't keep progress in
`self` between calls.


## Methods

### `init`

{/* init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)? */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
init(self: T, context: Context) -> boolean
```
</div>

### `transform`

{/* transform: (self: T, value: number) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
transform(self: T, value: number) -> number
```
</div>

Maps a linear progress `value` in 0..1 to an eased one.


### `transformValue`

{/* transformValue: (self: T, from: number, to: number, value: number) -> number */}
<div class="signature">
```lua
transformValue(self: T, from: number, to: number, value: number) -> number
```
</div>

Returns the value between `from` and `to` at linear progress `value`.
